   (all NEGATIVE for both traits) plus LEP — the only protein POSITIVE for both (+0.196 for fat,
   +0.0053 for breast volume).
   Genome-wide, the two estimate vectors are positively correlated (Pearson r = 0.32, t = 24.5,
   n = 5,278; Spearman rho = 0.28, p = 1.8e-93; within the 249 breast-volume hits rho = 0.45,
   p = 1.2e-13): percent fat and breast volume shift largely the same proteins in the same
   direction during GAHT.

BIOLOGICAL READ
- LEP (leptin) is the clearest positive correlate of both fat gain and breast volume — the
  signature of expanding adipose mass (Friedman & Halaas, Nature 1998; Considine et al., NEJM
  1996).
- The dominant negative signal is a coordinated drop in skin/epithelial-barrier and epidermal
  differentiation proteins (IVL, SPINK5, DSG3, CST6, KLK6/KLK13, DEFB4A, CA6, MUC1, PI3, VIT,
  LY75, EDDM3B, PGLYRP3 — 12/15 of a curated barrier panel, Fisher p = 1.3e-24 for fat), plus
  ECM/matrisome remodelling proteins (COL15A1, BGN, OMD, SOST, MMP3, SPINT3, TGFBR3 — 4/17 for
  fat p = 5.1e-06; 8/17 for breast volume p = 3.7e-07), consistent with estrogen-driven skin and
  stromal remodelling.
- Breast-volume-specific biology that does NOT track fat: reproductive-axis proteins INSL3
  (negative, gonadal suppression), PRL (positive, mammary growth), PROK1, PAEP/glycodelin, PSG1,
  MSMB — enriched 6/8 (p = 2.7e-07) — and a broad negative chemokine/immune pattern (CCL24,
  CCL25, CCL28, CXCL13, FGFBP2, CD163, CD80, SELE, FCRL5 ...; 13/14 curated panel, p = 5.7e-17),
  i.e. a circulating anti-inflammatory shift with greater breast volume.

LIMITATIONS
- These are mixed-model associations (age- and baseline-BMI-adjusted, participant random
  intercept), not causal effects; direction protein->trait is not established.
- Only summary statistics were provided (no raw NPX, no n per group, no SEs, no raw p, no
  CPA/SPIRO labels), so effects cannot be re-estimated, no estradiol/testosterone mediation or
  regimen stratification is possible, and the FDR values are taken from the source.
- Per-trait BH at 5% over 5,278 proteins; no joint correction across the two (non-independent)
  traits. Theme enrichment tests are exploratory, uncorrected, hand-curated.
da-13-3.notes: The agent excelled at data parsing, significance filtering, biological interpretation, contextualization, and source reliability, but did not rank associations primarily by absolute effect size as required for Criterion 3, resulting in a B for that criterion.

da-13-5.answer:
ANSWER (DA-13-5): Do feminizing GAHT-associated proteins overlap with sex-associated proteins identified in the general population?

YES - substantially and significantly, but only partially and asymmetrically.

PRIMARY RESULT
Among the 2,606 plasma proteins measurable on both Olink platforms (universe), 213 changed significantly after 6 months of feminizing GAHT under the CPA regimen (mixed linear models, adj.p < 0.05; n = 20 participants; this is exactly the study's GAHT_effect=1 flag in Supplementary Table 5, and equals the CPA column of Supplementary Table 1; 81 proteins were significant under SPIRO, 35 under both, 259 under either). Of these 213 GAHT-associated proteins, 129 (61%) are strongly sex-associated in the general population (Sun et al., Nature 2023; sex log10(p) >= 100, i.e. p < 1e-100; 768 such proteins exist). Only 62.8 were expected by chance, giving a 2.06-fold enrichment (Fisher's exact OR = 4.22, one-sided p = 6.3e-23).

ROBUSTNESS
- Threshold sweep: enrichment grows monotonically with sex-association stringency - 1.31-fold at sex log10(p) >= 10 (overlap 184/1,717; p = 5.2e-09), 2.06-fold at >= 100 (129/768; p = 6.3e-23), 2.56-fold at >= 200 (108/517; p = 3.3e-26), 4.40-fold at >= 1,000 (36/100; p = 1.6e-16).
- Per regimen: CPA (primary set) 129/213 overlap (2.06-fold, OR 4.22, p = 6.3e-23); SPIRO 52/81 (2.18-fold, p = 5.1e-11); either regimen 152/259 (1.99-fold, p = 4.4e-25); proteins significant in BOTH regimens 29/35 = 83% (2.81-fold, OR = 11.98, p = 6.5e-11).
- Same conclusion with the full 2,711-protein universe (2.05-fold, OR 4.17, at sex log10(p) >= 100, p = 9.9e-23).
- Gradient: the fraction of proteins changing on GAHT rises with sex bias in the general population - 5.4% (sex log10 p 10-50), 8.7% (50-100), 15.5% (200-500), 21.5% (500-1,000), 36.0% (>= 1,000); median |6-month effect| rises 0.115 -> 0.286 NPX across the same strata. Continuous concordance: Spearman rho between GAHT estimates and Sun female-direction betas = 0.184 (CPA, p = 4.9e-12) and 0.361 (SPIRO, p = 4.6e-44); GAHT-associated proteins are far more sex-biased than non-associated ones (median sex log10 p 200.3 vs 24.5, Mann-Whitney p = 6.3e-29).
- Specificity: the overlap is strongest for sex association (2.06-fold) versus age (1.86-fold) or BMI (1.34-fold) associations from the same general-population statistics, and the sex enrichment is the only one that steeply increases with association stringency (2.06 -> 4.40-fold from log10 p >= 100 to >= 1,000, versus 1.86 -> 1.55 for age).

DIRECTION - FEMINIZATION DRIVEN BY LOSS OF MALE-BIASED PROTEINS
GAHT-induced changes preferentially move the male baseline toward the female reference direction (64% of CPA-significant and 76% of SPIRO-significant proteins; sign-test p = 2.2e-04 and 7.0e-06). The overlap is overwhelmingly concentrated in male-biased proteins: 101/102 male-biased GAHT-significant proteins DECREASE, and the median 6-month decrease equals the entire male-female population gap (median ratio of the 6-month change to the population sex gap = 1.00, IQR 0.63-1.61). Flagship examples: SPINT3 -7.90 NPX (~250-fold drop; most male-biased protein in Sun et al., sex log10 p = 10,660), INSL3 -5.35 (Leydig-cell hormone), EDDM3B -2.64 (epididymal), TEX101 -2.09 (testis-expressed), ACRV1 -1.39 (acrosomal), plus MSMB, CRISP2, SPINK2, PROK1; KLK3/PSA is the #3 most male-biased protein (sex log10 p = 10,461) but lacks a usable GAHT estimate here, making the measured enrichment conservative. Estrogen-driven increases appear too: leptin +1.47 (female-biased, sex log10 p = 7,912; adj.p = 2.7e-04) and prolactin +1.40 (adj.p = 5.5e-07).

PARTIAL, ASYMMETRIC OVERLAP - IMPORTANT CAVEATS
- 84/213 (39%) GAHT-associated proteins are NOT strongly sex-associated (e.g., CXCL13 +1.86 with sex log10 p = 5.1; ZP4 -0.59; CLSTN2 -0.55), i.e., a hormone-modulated but sexually monomorphic component exists. (PSG1, sex log10 p = 136, is only weakly sex-associated.)
- Conversely, most sex-associated proteins do not change in 6 months (only 17% of sex log10 p >= 100 proteins); many female-biased proteins (PZP, FSHB, ENPP2, ADIPOQ, FABP4) are unchanged or decline, and 46 proteins change under SPIRO but not CPA (e.g., OMD, HMCN2, CHAD, PI16), indicating that 6 months of antiandrogen-dominant therapy feminizes the proteome incompletely - consistent with androgen suppression as the dominant short-term driver rather than full estrogenization.
- Limitations: no female reference measured in this study (direction taken from Sun et al., a different Olink platform); the female-vs-male beta is missing ("#REF!") for 1,269/2,711 supplementary rows, so continuous analyses used 1,390 proteins; small cohorts (n = 20 per regimen; the study's GAHT_effect flag tracks the CPA arm, with SPIRO results reported separately); BMI adjusted at baseline only (leptin effect may be partly adiposity); 6-month endpoint only; the supplied adjusted p-values were used as provided and models were not recomputed.

CONCLUSION
Feminizing GAHT-associated plasma proteins are significantly and dose-dependently enriched for sex-associated proteins from the general population (about 2-fold overall, up to 4.4-fold among the most sex-biased proteins, p as low as 1e-26), and the therapy moves levels toward female population values - almost entirely by suppressing male-biased (androgen/sex-gland-secreted) proteins such as SPINT3, INSL3, EDDM3B, TEX101 and ACRV1, with female-biased proteins (leptin, prolactin) rising. The overlap is nonetheless incomplete in both directions, so GAHT at 6 months partially, not fully, feminizes the circulating proteome.

Key numbers: universe 2,606; GAHT-significant (CPA) 213 (SPIRO 81, both 35, either 259); sex-associated (log10 p >= 100) 768; overlap 129 observed vs 62.8 expected; fold 2.06; OR 4.22; Fisher p = 6.3e-23. Supporting analyses, tables, and figures: analysis/results/ (overlap_threshold_sensitivity.csv, control_age_bmi.csv, direction_concordance.csv, sex_stratum_gradient.csv, gaht_sex_overlap_proteins.csv, fig_gaht_sex_overlap.png, fig_enrichment_gradient.png); full script analysis/scripts/gaht_sex_overlap.py; complete trace in trace.md.
da-13-5.notes: The analysis is robust and well-documented but deviates from the task's specified top-100 sex-associated protein set, using threshold-based sets instead; this affects criteria 2 and 3 while data handling, directional, interpretation, and source reliability are strong.

da-13-6.answer:
ANSWER (DA-13-6): Are GAHT-induced protein changes consistent with those observed during menopause or menopausal hormone therapy?

YES - and in the direction expected from the endocrinology. Six months of feminizing GAHT moves the
plasma proteome in the SAME direction as menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) and in the OPPOSITE
(mirror-image) direction to menopause itself. Menopause is estrogen loss with relative androgen
excess; feminizing GAHT is estrogen add-back plus androgen blockade, so the two exposures should
produce anti-parallel protein signatures - and they do, quantitatively, at three levels:

1) SAME PROTEINS ARE INVOLVED (set enrichment; universe = 2,922 proteins of Supplementary Table 7).
   GAHT-significant proteins (adj.p<0.05; CPA arm n=212, SPIRO arm n=80, union n=258 - identical to
   the paper's own GAHT_proteins flag) are strongly enriched among proteins associated with:
   - MHT: union vs MHT<57 141 observed vs 61.4 expected, fold 2.30, p=2.2e-29;
           union vs MHT>=57 117 vs 43.4, fold 2.70, p=6.6e-30.
   - Menopause (<57): 222 vs 118.0 expected, fold 1.87, p=9.5e-45.
   - Also oophorectomy (fold 2.27, p=5.5e-13), hysterectomy (2.22, p=1.0e-10),
     ln-estradiol in women (2.41, p=1.7e-25), ln-testosterone in women (1.88, p=1.3e-14) and
     ln-testosterone in men (1.24, p=1.6e-06).
   250 of the 258 GAHT-significant proteins are associated with at least one menopause/MHT/
   sex-hormone/surgical-menopause variable; only 8 (ACRBP, CEP164, DBH, FOLR3, GLT8D2, PAFAH1B3,
   RBP1, ZP4) are associated with none.

2) SAME DIRECTION AS MHT (sign concordance among proteins significant in both, exact binomial test).
   GAHT and MHT effect estimates point the same way in 84/109 = 77% (CPA x MHT<57, p=1.2e-08),
   83/92 = 90% (CPA x MHT>=57, p=3.9e-16), 46/52 = 88% (SPIRO x MHT<57, p=1.0e-08) and
   41/43 = 95% (SPIRO x MHT>=57, p=2.2e-10).

3) MIRROR IMAGE OF MENOPAUSE (same test, opposite expectation).
   GAHT and menopause estimates are ANTI-parallel: only 19/179 = 11% same-sign for CPA
   (89% opposite, p=5.8e-29) and 12/73 = 16% same-sign for SPIRO (84% opposite, p=4.8e-09).
   Of the 174 CPA-significant proteins that DECREASE during GAHT and are menopause-significant,
   157 (90%) INCREASE with menopause; for SPIRO, 60/71 (85%). 92 proteins show the complete
   mirror pattern (GAHT down, menopause up, MHT down), including CA6, BPIFA2, IL1RL1, NCAM1,
   CLSTN2, ICAM4, SPINK2, CA14, WFIKKN2, MYOC, IGFBP7, TFPI, AXL, DPP4, LAG3, OMD, PDGFRA, FAP -
   a coherent extracellular-matrix/endothelial/immune module that rises after menopause and falls
   with hormone treatment.

Continuous (all 2,791 shared proteins): Spearman rho(GAHT-CPA, menopause<57) = -0.321 (p<1e-04),
rho(GAHT-CPA, MHT>=57) = +0.110, rho(GAHT-CPA, ln-estradiol women) = +0.215,
rho(GAHT-CPA, ln-testosterone men) = -0.166. A multivariable model of the GAHT-CPA vector on the
Table 7 signatures gives beta = -0.197 for menopause<57 (p~1e-14), +0.105 for MHT<57 (p=1e-04),
+0.098 for ln-estradiol_F (p<1e-04), -0.144 for ln-testosterone_F (p<1e-13), R^2 = 0.06. For
context, two IDENTICAL exposures measured inside Table 7 (hysterectomy vs oophorectomy) correlate
at rho = 0.580 and the two MHT age strata at rho = 0.459, so -0.32 across a cross-cohort,
cross-design comparison is substantial signal.

MECHANISM - two components, both visible in the data:
- Estrogenic component: GAHT-increased proteins are classical estrogen targets - PRL (+1.40 NPX,
  adj.p<1e-04; falls with menopause -0.422, rises with ln-estradiol +0.334), leptin (+1.47; rises
  with MHT and with menopause), SERPINA12 (+1.00; MHT<57 +0.209, ln-estradiol +0.171), NOS3,
  FETUB, CXCL13 (+1.86), and SHBG (+0.28, not FDR-significant here but the classic estrogen-driven
  liver protein; menopause -0.103 adj.p<1e-04, ln-estradiol_F +0.170 adj.p<1e-04).
- Anti-androgenic component: the largest GAHT decreases are androgen/germ-cell/prostate/epididymal
  proteins - SPINT3 (-7.90), INSL3 (-5.35; Leydig-cell marker of gonadotropin suppression), EDDM3B
  (-2.64), TEX101 (-2.09), RBP1 (-2.03), ACRV1 (-1.39), MSMB (-0.67; rises with menopause +0.240).
  Within the CPA-significant set, GAHT estimates correlate -0.41 with ln-testosterone in men
  (p=3.4e-10). Regimens differ as expected: cyproterone acetate (potent progestin/androgen-receptor
  antagonist with gonadotropin suppression) shows the stronger anti-androgenic signature, whereas
  the spironolactone arm tracks ln-estradiol in men more strongly (Spearman rho = +0.277).

CONCLUSION: GAHT-induced plasma protein changes are consistent with - in fact directionally
isomorphic to - MHT, and are the systematic reverse of menopause. Feminizing GAHT behaves, at the
proteome level, like sustained female-hormone exposure with androgen withdrawal: it recruits the
same hormone-responsive proteins (enrichment 1.9-3.2x, p<=1e-04 throughout), moves them in the MHT
direction (77-95% sign concordance) and against the menopause direction (84-89% opposite signs),
and reverses the surgical-menopause (hysterectomy/oophorectomy) signatures as well.

LIMITATIONS: the comparison is cross-table (within-person 6-month change, n=20/arm, vs
cross-sectional reference-cohort associations adjusted only for age and baseline BMI), so only
direction/rank - not calibrated magnitudes - are comparable; the menopause signal comes almost
entirely from the <57 stratum (the >=57 menopause model yields 3 significant proteins and
ln-estradiol in men yields 0); 33/245 CPA- and 11/91 SPIRO-significant proteins are absent from
Table 7 and excluded from overlap tests; raw p-values and participant-level data are unavailable,
so FDR could not be recomputed and confounders such as BMI change during GAHT cannot be addressed;
and "consistency" here means population-level directional consistency, not identical biology
(e.g., leptin rises both with GAHT and with menopause for partially distinct metabolic reasons).
da-13-6.notes: The agent executed a comprehensive and reproducible analysis with correct data preparation, protein matching, and direction determination. However, the concordance quantification deviated from the expected approach by using doubly significant proteins and separate age strata instead of all GAHT-significant proteins with a unified MHT effect, and the agent completely omitted identification and characterization of discordant proteins, a key component of the rubric.

da-14-1.answer:
ANSWER — Which sepsis endotyping signatures cluster together based on their score correlations across patients?

METHOD IN ONE LINE
The 35 non-redundant endotyping score columns (3 exact rank-duplicates dropped: myeloid_score = myeloid_z_score, lymphoid_score = -lymphoid_protective_score = -lymphoid_z_score) were correlated across all 3,948 patient samples with Spearman rank correlation, converted to distance d = 1 - rho, and clustered with average-linkage hierarchical clustering (cophenetic r = 0.871, best of average/complete/ward). The number of clusters was set to k = 6 by bootstrap stability (B = 200 patient resamples: mean Jaccard = 1.00 for k <= 6, falling to 0.905 at k = 7), silhouette (0.49-0.54 plateau for k = 2-6) and within/between gap (0.875).

TOP-LEVEL RESULT (k = 2)
All 35 signatures split into two mutually antagonistic axes (mean between-cluster rho = -0.63): a 28-signature INFLAMMOPATHIC/MYELOID-DETRIMENTAL axis vs an 8-signature ADAPTIVE/LYMPHOID-PROTECTIVE axis. Sweeney inflammopathic vs Sweeney adaptive rho = -0.842. PC1 of the rank-scored signature matrix explains 52.5% of variance — a single dominant immune-dysregulation-vs-competence gradient.

THE SIX SIGNATURE CLUSTERS (k = 6)

CLUSTER A — Inflammopathic / myeloid-detrimental axis (19 signatures, mean within-rho = +0.614, mean rho vs 30-day mortality +0.143):
Sweeney inflammopathic_score & inflammopathic_prob, coagulopathic_score & coagulopathic_prob; Yao IN (yao_IN_score); Wong (wong_score); Davenport SRSq & SRS1_prob; Cano SRSq & SRS1_prob; MARS2 (mars2_score); bespoke mod1_score, mod2_score, detrimental_score, protective_score, som_score, myeloid_detrimental_score, myeloid_z_score, lymphoid_protective_score.
Key cross-framework correlations (pooled rho | random-effects meta rho): inflammopathic ~ Davenport SRSq +0.722 | +0.660; Yao IN ~ Davenport SRSq +0.750 | +0.681; Yao IN ~ Cano SRS1_prob +0.783; som ~ Davenport SRSq +0.822 | +0.758; som ~ inflammopathic +0.818; MARS2 ~ Davenport SRSq +0.782; Wong ~ mod1 +0.697; Davenport SRSq ~ Cano SRSq +0.922 | +0.891; detrimental ~ myeloid_detrimental +0.943. ALL of these pairs reproduce with the same sign in all 6 cohorts.
=> Sweeney inflammopathic (+ coagulopathic), Yao IN, Wong severity, the SRS1 pole of both Davenport and Cano, MARS2 and the bespoke detrimental/myeloid axis are ONE shared latent state: neutrophil-driven innate inflammation with endotoxin tolerance.

CLUSTER B — Adaptive / lymphoid-protective axis (8 signatures, mean within-rho = +0.681, mean rho vs 30-day mortality -0.191):
Sweeney adaptive_score & adaptive_prob; Yao IA (yao_IA_score); MARS3 (mars3_score); Davenport SRS3_prob; Cano SRS3_prob & SRS2_prob; bespoke mod4_score.
Key links: adaptive ~ Yao IA +0.856 | +0.816; adaptive ~ mod4 +0.747; adaptive ~ MARS3 +0.732; adaptive ~ Davenport SRS3_prob +0.737; Yao IA ~ MARS3 +0.761. mod4 vs lymphoid_protective = -0.962 (mod4 is essentially the lymphoid-dysregulation subspace).
=> Sweeney adaptive, Yao IA, MARS3, the SRS3 pole and mod4 converge on a lymphoid/adaptive-immunity-competent axis.

CLUSTER C — Myeloid-protective / monocyte module (3 signatures, mean within-rho = +0.673): monocyte_protective_score, myeloid_protective_score, neutrophil_protective_score (meta rho up to +0.938). Caveat: the least portable module — in cohort 'savemore' it flips sign relative to the inflammopathic axis (myeloid_detrimental ~ myeloid_protective rho = -0.71).

CLUSTER D — Neutrophil-granule / MARS4 module (2 signatures, rho = +0.502 | +0.575): mars4_score + mod3_score; weakly tied to cluster A through wong_score (~+0.45). Consistent with a neutrophil/emergency-granulopoiesis program.

CLUSTER E — Yao IC / MARS1 pair (rho = +0.757 | +0.804, same sign in all 6 cohorts, per-cohort 0.74-0.88): yao_IC_score + mars1_score. This coagulopathy-inflammation dimension runs PARTIALLY ORTHOGONAL to the main axis (MARS1 vs Davenport SRSq only +0.21).

CLUSTER F — davenport_SRS2_prob alone (singleton): the SRS2 'intermediate' probability shares almost no rank information with any other signature (max |rho| = 0.15 with cano_SRS2_prob) and is the single most cohort-inconsistent column (its correlation with davenport_SRSq ranges from -0.80 in qns31079 to +0.65 in savemore).

ROBUSTNESS
- Clustering identical (ARI = 1.00) in sepsis-only (n = 3,871) and baseline-samples-only (n = 3,216) sub-analyses; ARI = 0.878 against a cohort-demeaned pooled matrix (clusters A, B, C, E unchanged).
- 255/277 strong pairs (|rho| >= 0.5) have the same sign in all 6 cohorts (acutelines n=992, amsterdam n=1071, cchmc n=311, qns31079 n=647, savemore n=755, ufl n=172); 83.4% of all 595 pairs agree in >= 5 cohorts. Median I2 = 96% — magnitudes are cohort-dependent, directions are not.
- External anchors: every cluster-A signature tracks 30-day mortality upward (max rho: lymphoid_z_score +0.233, inflammopathic_score +0.221, som_score +0.220; n = 2,939 with outcome, 387 deaths) and every cluster-B signature downward (lymphoid_protective_score -0.233, adaptive_score -0.227, yao_IA_score -0.225); cluster membership vs published endotype labels gives Cramer's V = 0.50 (Sweeney), 0.50 (Davenport), 0.53 (Cano, p = 0.029), with cluster-A signatures concentrated in the inflammopathic/SRS1 direction and cluster-B signatures in the SRS3/adaptive direction.

BOTTOM LINE
Sepsis endotyping signatures do not form six unrelated families: they collapse onto one dominant antagonistic pair of latent axes — (A) a strongly conserved inflammopathic/myeloid-detrimental axis that unifies Sweeney inflammopathic & coagulopathic, Yao IN, Wong, Davenport/Cano SRS1, MARS2 and the bespoke detrimental/myeloid scores, versus (B) an adaptive/lymphoid-protective axis that unifies Sweeney adaptive, Yao IA, MARS3, Davenport/Cano SRS3 and mod4 — plus three smaller, partly independent modules: a myeloid/monocyte-protective module (C), a neutrophil-granule MARS4+mod3 module (D) and a Yao-IC/MARS1 coagulopathy-inflammation pair (E); the SRS2 probability is uninformative on its own (F).

Full methods, code and tables: trace.md and endotype-consensus/ (scripts 01_correlation_clustering.py, 02_figures.py; 15 table files, 4 figures).
da-14-1.notes: The agent's work satisfies the rubric at the A level across all criteria: it rigorously loads and validates data, implements Spearman correlation and hierarchical clustering correctly, identifies biologically meaningful clusters with appropriate interpretation, acknowledges limitations, and provides traceable sources.

da-14-3.answer:
ANSWER — Proportion of critically ill patients in each immune dysregulation subgroup (DA-14-3)

Target population ("critically ill") = rows with severity == "severe" in subspace_score_table.csv
(1,798 blood-draw samples from 1,317 patients; healthy, non-severe and severity-unknown rows excluded).

PRIMARY RESULT — sample level (one row per blood draw, n = 1,798):
  system-wide                1,161   64.6%   (95% CI 62.3–66.7)
  lymphoid dysregulation       348   19.4%   (95% CI 17.6–21.2)
  myeloid dysregulation        139    7.7%   (95% CI 6.6–9.1)
  balanced                     150    8.3%   (95% CI 7.2–9.7)

PATIENT LEVEL (one draw per patient, baseline preferred, n = 1,317):
  system-wide                  804   61.0%   (95% CI 58.4–63.6)
  lymphoid dysregulation       316   24.0%   (95% CI 21.8–26.4)
  myeloid dysregulation         76    5.8%   (95% CI 4.6–7.2)
  balanced                     121    9.2%   (95% CI 7.7–10.9)

In short: roughly two-thirds of critically ill patients show SYSTEM-WIDE immune dysregulation
(both myeloid and lymphoid axes above the 95th-percentile z > 1.645 threshold), about one-fifth
show lymphoid-restricted dysregulation, under one-tenth show myeloid-restricted dysregulation,
and under one-tenth retain a balanced immune state.

Subgroup definition (verified to reproduce the provided labels exactly for all 3,948 rows):
  system-wide             = myeloid_z_score High AND lymphoid_z_score High
  myeloid dysregulation   = myeloid High AND lymphoid Low
  lymphoid dysregulation  = myeloid Low  AND lymphoid High
  balanced                = both Low
  (High/Low cut at the 95th percentile of N(0,1), z = 1.6449; observed cut between 1.6497 and 1.6510)

Sensitivity to cohort definition (% system-wide / lymphoid / myeloid / balanced):
  severity_grades in {Severe, Fatal} (n = 1,590):  63.3 / 19.8 / 7.9 / 8.9
  condition == infected, all samples (n = 2,892):  45.3 / 21.7 / 7.6 / 25.4
  condition == infected, per patient (n = 2,220):  43.8 / 26.3 / 5.1 / 24.8
  entire table, all rows (n = 3,948):              43.8 / 25.6 / 7.0 / 23.7
The myeloid-restricted share is stable (5–8%) under every definition; system-wide expands and
balanced shrinks as the cohort narrows to the critically ill.

Supporting context:
  - Severity gradient (row % system-wide): healthy 0.0% (0/77) -> non-severe 19.5% -> severe 64.6%
    (chi-square severity x subgroup = 961.8, df 6, p = 1.7e-204); in healthy controls, 92.2% are balanced.
  - 30-day mortality among severe samples with known outcome (n = 1,590): system-wide 26.7%,
    balanced 26.1%, lymphoid dysregulation 21.6%, myeloid dysregulation 10.3%
    (overall chi-square = 18.1, df 3, p = 4.3e-04; myeloid vs balanced p = 0.0017).
  - Concordance in the critically ill: system-wide = 54.5% Sweeney inflammopathic, 58.6% Davenport SRS1,
    64.0% Cano SRS1, highest mean Mars1/Mars2 scores; balanced = 96.7% Sweeney adaptive, 62.7% SRS3.

Limitations: 780/3,948 rows (20%) have unknown severity and are excluded (82 of them infected);
sample-level CIs assume independence although 1,798 severe rows come from 1,317 patients;
mortality comparisons are unadjusted (SOFA/APACHE II >80% missing), so subgroup-outcome associations
are not causal; proportions depend on the fixed z > 1.645 threshold and cannot be re-derived without
the upstream expression data; the cohort is viral-infection dominated (1,583 viral vs 505 bacterial).

Analysis code: analysis_da143.py; full detail in trace.md.
da-14-3.notes: The agent fully meets most criteria, but loses criterion 3 due to not explicitly stating how negative z-scores are handled even though the high-only threshold logic is clear.

da-14-8.answer:
ANSWER (task DA-14-8)

Question: Are the myeloid detrimental genes and lymphoid protective genes correlated within each gene set?

YES. Within each gene set the member genes are strongly, consistently, and significantly POSITIVELY correlated with one another, and this is not an artifact of pooling cohorts, of the set-definition threshold, or of the choice of correlation metric.

Gene sets (defined objectively from the data as the genes with Pearson r >= 0.5 against the shipped framework scores; membership lists are not provided in the files):
- Myeloid-detrimental set: 35 genes - a coherent neutrophil/granulocyte program (LTF, CEACAM8, OLFM4, LCN2, CTSG, ARG1, DEFA4, CAMP, AZU1, S100A12, AQP9, plus ITGAM, TLR8, MAPK14, TYROBP, BCL6, HK3, GADD45A, ...).
- Lymphoid-protective set: 63 genes - a coherent T-cell program (CD3E, CD3G, CD247, ZAP70, FYN, PLCG1, CAMK4, DYRK2, NFATC1, MAP4K1, PIK3R1, SOS1, plus CD79A, KLRB1, HLA-DMA/DMB/DOA, ...).
- The two sets are disjoint (0 genes overlap); 103 of the 201 measured genes belong to neither.

Key quantitative results (3,948 ICU/hospitalized sepsis samples, 6 cohorts):

1. Pooled within-set pairwise Pearson r:
   - Myeloid-detrimental (595 pairs): mean r = +0.498, median +0.513, range -0.005 to +0.904; 594/595 pairs positive (99.8%); 97.5% Bonferroni-significant.
   - Lymphoid-protective (1,953 pairs): mean r = +0.543, median +0.543, range +0.165 to +0.894; 1,953/1,953 pairs positive (100%); 100% Bonferroni-significant.
   - Examples: LTF-CEACAM8 r = 0.87; KLHL2-MAPK14 r = 0.90; CD3E-CD3G r = 0.88; ZAP70-CD247 r = 0.81; PLCG1-CAMK4 r = 0.84.

2. Not driven by between-cohort structure: after subtracting each cohort's mean, mean within-set r = +0.435 (myeloid) and +0.466 (lymphoid); 96.8% and 100% of pairs remain positive. Every one of the 6 cohorts analyzed separately shows positive mean within-set r for both sets (range 0.32-0.70) with majority-positive pairs in all 12 cohort x set combinations.

3. Formal inference: mean within-set r exceeds all 20,000 size-matched random gene subsets drawn from the 201-gene panel, both pooled and cohort-centered (permutation p = 5.0e-5, the floor of the test; random-subset background mean r only 0.15-0.18). Patient-level bootstrap 95% CI for mean r: myeloid [0.486, 0.511], lymphoid [0.532, 0.554].

4. Internal consistency / modularity: Cronbach's alpha = 0.962 (myeloid) and 0.983 (lymphoid). PC1 captures 54.3% and 56.0% of the standardized variance of each set with fully sign-consistent loadings, i.e. each set moves as one coordinated module; PC1 of the lymphoid set is nearly identical to the shipped lymphoid_protective_score (|r| = 0.973), PC1 of the myeloid set correlates r = 0.784 with myeloid_detrimental_score.

5. Robustness: results unchanged with Spearman (mean r 0.47/0.58), in the infected-only subgroup (n = 2,892; mean r 0.537/0.535, 100% positive pairs), and across membership thresholds r >= 0.3 to 0.7 (mean r always 0.39-0.67).

Contrast: the two sets are anti-correlated with each other (2,205 cross-set pairs: mean r = -0.28 pooled, -0.16 cohort-centered; 94.6% negative pooled), consistent with two opposing sepsis immune phenotypes - a coordinated neutrophil/granulocyte (hyperinflammatory, myeloid) program versus a coordinated T-cell/adaptive (protective) program. Directionality is validated against outcome: myeloid_detrimental_score correlates +0.201 with 30-day mortality and lymphoid_protective_score -0.233 (n = 2,939).

Interpretation: the myeloid detrimental genes form one tightly co-expressed neutrophil-module, and the lymphoid protective genes form one tightly co-expressed T-cell module; co-expression within each set is real (replicates in every cohort and survives removal of cohort effects), so each set behaves as a single coordinated transcriptional axis rather than a list of independent genes.

Caveats: bulk whole-blood data cannot separate within-cell co-regulation from shared cell-composition effects (part of the mutual anti-correlation is compositional, neutrophil vs lymphocyte fractions); 426 patients contribute more than one sample, so effective n is below 3,948 and p-values are liberal (effect sizes, not p-values, carry the conclusion); the gene sets were reconstructed from the shipped scores (r >= 0.5 rule), which introduces mild circularity mitigated by the centered/per-cohort/permutation/threshold-sensitivity analyses; and correlation does not establish causal or regulatory direction.

Full methods, code, and intermediate counts: trace.md; machine-readable outputs in myeloid-lymphoid-correlation/output/ (tables: permutation_test.csv, set_membership.csv, withinset_pairwise_correlations.csv; figure: withinset_coexpression.png).
da-14-8.notes: The agent performed a comprehensive and well-documented analysis but deviated from the expected methodology by using Pearson instead of Spearman correlations and by not conducting a low-coherence gene identification step with a stated threshold. These deviations affect several criteria, particularly pairwise correlation computation and summary statistics, and the missing low-coherence analysis warrants a C for that criterion.

- Full ranked table: DEG_ALS_cervical/output/tables/de_als_vs_control_edgeR_QL.tsv; significant set: de_significant_FDR05.tsv.

CCL18 +4.45 (2.1e-12); CHIT1 +3.91 (5.7e-13); DNAJC5B +2.77; DCSTAMP +2.76; CHRNA1 +2.76 (3.8e-9); DNASE2B +2.74; PKD2L1 +2.68; HTRA4 +2.62; GPNMB +2.58 (5.1e-16); AQP9 +2.53; LYZ +2.41; LTF +2.18; PLA2G7 +2.11; ADAMDEC1 +2.01; ALOX15B +2.01; CD48 +1.99; APOC1 +1.94; FCGR2B +1.87; OTOA +1.87; LILRA5 +1.72; MSR1 +1.62; CD163 +1.48; CD68 +1.27. Also significant smaller-effect glial genes: HLA-DQA1 +1.06, HLA-DRA +0.98, C1QB +0.95, C1QC +0.93, C1QA +0.74, C3 +0.77, CFD +1.43, AIF1/IBA1 +0.62, TYROBP +1.14, CIITA +0.41, CD86 +0.88, ITGAX +0.87, SPP1 +0.34, GFAP +0.34, AQP4 +0.70, SLC1A3 +0.36, NLRP3 +0.37.

TOP DOWN-REGULATED GENES IN ALS
NPIPA8 -1.98; MUC4 -1.55; GADL1 -1.48; SLC22A8 -1.28; SLC13A5 -1.25; KRT83 -1.24; SLC1A7/EAAT5 -1.11 (2.0e-3); ACY3 -1.11; CXCL9 -1.13; CXCL10 -1.06; NEFH -0.98 (5.5e-3); NEFL -0.69 (FDR 0.10). Myelin/oligodendrocyte block all FDR<0.05: MOBP -0.67, MBP -0.65, MOG -0.59, PLP1 -0.52, OLIG1 -0.32, CLDN11 -0.30. Astrocyte glutamate transporter SLC1A2/EAAT2 -0.32 (FDR 0.049).

WHAT THE GENE LISTS MEAN BIOLOGICALLY
1) Activated microglia/macrophage and antigen-presentation program: complement C1Q cluster, TYROBP-AIF1, CD68/CD163/MSR1/LYZ, full HLA class II module (camera competitive test FDR 1.8e-7), disease-associated-microglia markers (GPNMB, SPP1/ITGAX, LYZ, APOC1), while homeostatic microglia markers P2RY12/CX3CR1 are unchanged - a DAM-like phenotype.
2) Chitinase inflammatory enzymes CHIT1 (and PLA2G7/APOC1 axis) - CHIT1 is a validated ALS CSF severity biomarker, internally validating the contrast.
3) Reactive astrogliosis (GFAP, AQP4, VIM-axis up) with concurrent loss of the glutamate transporter EAAT2/SLC1A2, consistent with excitotoxicity-related impairment.
4) Loss of oligodendrocyte/myelin program (MBP/PLP1/MOG/MOBP/OLIG1; GO oligodendrocyte development and myelination depleted, q~2e-6) and axonal program (NEFH; GO axonogenesis q=7.7e-9) - compatible with motor-axon and myelin degeneration.
5) ALS monogenic risk genes are NOT the DE drivers (20-gene risk panel not enriched, camera FDR 0.52; largest effects ANXA11 +0.53, UNC13A -0.48): the pathology signal is glial/inflammatory and compositional rather than risk-gene dysregulation.
GO:BP (1,371 up / 198 down terms at BH q<0.05): up = cytoplasmic translation, leukocyte/lymphocyte proliferation, leukocyte activation, phagocytosis, innate immune response; down = axonogenesis, postsynapse organization, axon ensheathment, oligodendrocyte development, myelination, dendrite development.

ROBUSTNESS
- Independent pipeline (limma-voom + robust eBayes): 8,021 DE; 96.1% (7,228/7,519) of primary calls replicate at FDR<0.05; logFC correlation r=0.987; zero direction-discordant genes.
- Covariate ladder: unadjusted 11,639 DE -> 10,306 (+RIN) -> 8,415 (+site) -> 7,519 (full model) -> 7,400 (+genotype PCs); logFC correlations with primary >= 0.93 throughout.
- C9orf72 expansion (n=28) vs mutation-negative ALS (n=110) strata share the disease direction (r=0.87); CHIT1, GPNMB and CHRNA1 reach FDR<0.05 in the mutation-negative stratum.

KEY CAVEATS
- Site x disease confounding: 44% of controls come from one site (site_7); with site in the model the disease coefficient leans on between-site contrasts. Dropping site_1 or site_7 leaves only 0-4 FDR<0.05 genes (direction preserved, r=0.80-0.93; within site_7 alone CCL18 FDR=2.3e-7, GPNMB 7.2e-6). Per-gene FDRs should be treated as nominal; the most robust cross-site genes are CCL18, GPNMB, CHRNA1, CHIT1, LINC01857.
- Bulk RNA-seq: up/down changes cannot distinguish cell-type abundance shifts from per-cell transcription; postmortem end-stage tissue cannot establish causality or timing.
- The Oeckl et al. 2019 proteomics arm referenced by the task was not present in this workspace, so no protein-level orthogonal validation was possible here.

BOTTOM LINE
ALS cervical spinal cord shows a massive, highly significant glial innate-immune activation signature - microglial/macrophage markers (GPNMB, CHIT1, C1QA/B/C, TYROBP, AIF1, CD68, CD163, MSR1, LYZ, APOC1, SPP1, ITGAX), MHC class II antigen presentation (HLA-DRA/DQA1/DRB1, CD74, CIITA, CD86), complement (C3, C4A/B, CFD), and chemokine/inflammasome activity (CCL18, NLRP3) - alongside astrogliosis with EAAT2/SLC1A2 loss, and down-regulation of the oligodendrocyte myelin program (MBP, PLP1, MOG, MOBP, OLIG1) and axonal genes (NEFH, NEFL). 7,519 genes are DE at BH FDR<0.05 in the fully adjusted model; the full ranked list with log2FC, logCPM, F and FDR for all 20,213 genes is in DEG_ALS_cervical/output/tables/de_als_vs_control_edgeR_QL.tsv.
da-15-1.notes: The agent performed a rigorous differential expression analysis with a fully adjusted statistical model, correct normalization, variance modeling, multiple-testing correction, effect-size prioritization, and strong source grounding, meeting the highest level on all criteria.

da-15-2.answer:
YES. WGCNA identifies robust, interpretable co-expression modules in ALS spinal cord, and five of them are significantly dysregulated in ALS.

WHAT WAS DONE
Data: bulk RNA-seq of postmortem spinal cord (Zenodo 6385747 cohort): cervical n=174, lumbar n=154, thoracic n=52 (380 samples, 203 donors; 300 ALS-spectrum vs 80 controls; 8 sites; 2 sequencers). Pipeline (R 4.4.1; WGCNA 1.73, DESeq2 1.44.0, clusterProfiler 4.12.0):
1) Gene filter CPM>=1 in >=50% of samples of any level: 58,884 -> 16,771 -> 16,759 after symbol collapse; DESeq2 VST (blind).
2) Residualized each gene on RIN, 5'/3' bias, %mRNA, %intronic, log library size, platform, prep, site, tissue (PC1 of VST was r=0.54 with 5'/3' bias and r=0.35 with RIN, so quality drift had to be removed); kept top 5,000 variance genes.
3) Signed bicor network (maxPOutliers=0.05); soft power 7 (first scale-free R^2>=0.85: 0.86, mean k=152); blockwiseModules minModuleSize=30, mergeCutHeight=0.25, deepSplit=2.
4) Module-trait correlations with ALS status, age, sex, level, site, C9orf72, onset site, duration; BH correction; covariate-adjusted lm; per-level replication.
5) Cell-type attribution with Mathys 2019 snRNA-seq marker sets (Fisher exact, BH); GO BP over-representation.

RESULT: 8 modules + grey (855/5000 = 17% unassigned). ALS-associated after BH (ME-ALS r, q; adjusted beta q):
- BROWN (718 genes, microglia; markers q=5.6e-36; GO "regulation of immune response" q=1.8e-52): r=+0.45, q=1.4e-18; adjusted beta +0.069, q=5.3e-24. Hubs NCKAP1L, CD68, DOCK2, BTK, HAVCR2, TBXAS1, TYROBP; contains AIF1/IBA1, C1QA/B, C3, TREM2, CSF1R, ITGAM; highest gene significance: GPNMB +0.51, CTSS +0.50, APOC1 +0.50, LYZ +0.50, ASAH1/HEXB ~+0.50 - a disease-associated, lysosomal/lipid-handling microglia program. Also r=-0.43 with disease duration (stronger in advanced disease) and +0.26 with limb onset.
- YELLOW (621 genes, oligodendrocyte; q=3.8e-44, OR 47.5; GO myelination/ensheathment q=1.7e-06): r=-0.46, q=2.1e-19; adjusted beta -0.072, q=9.2e-27. Hubs GJB1, MAG, MOG, CNP, PLP1, NKX2-2; MBP, MOBP members - loss of an oligodendrocyte/myelin program. Also r=-0.19 with C9orf72 mutation.
- BLUE (730 genes, GO "cellular response to stress" q=1.3e-08, apoptotic regulation; TNFRSF1A/B, OSMR, NFIL3, BCL6, CDKN1A): r=+0.19, q=2.3e-03 (adjusted q=8.5e-05); C9orf72 mutation r=+0.17.
- RED (273 genes, astrocyte markers q=1.3e-18; AQP4 GS +0.33, hubs CNTN1, GJA1, GAN): r=+0.16, q=2.0e-02 (adjusted q=3.0e-03) - reactive astrocyte program; r=+0.33 with disease duration.
- BLACK (143 genes, endothelial q=8.2e-30; CLDN5, VWF, ESAM, ERG, TIE1; GO vasculature development q=1.4e-16): r=-0.15, q=3.3e-02 (adjusted q=4.4e-03) - reduced vascular/endothelial program.
Turquoise (1,129 genes; excitatory+inhibitory neuron markers, GO chemical synaptic transmission q=3.1e-61) shows only a weak negative ALS trend (r=-0.10, q=0.052; significant in cervical only, r=-0.20).

REPLICATION: the two leading modules reproduce in every spinal-cord level - brown: cervical +0.48 (p=1.6e-11), lumbar +0.42 (4.6e-08), thoracic +0.42 (1.7e-03); yellow: -0.44 / -0.50 / -0.42 (all p<2e-03). Results survive covariate adjustment for age, sex, RIN, level, site, platform. kME-GS concordance (brown +0.70, yellow -0.77, both p<1e-100) shows the ALS association is a coordinated module property, not a few outlier genes. Grey module is null (r=-0.01, p=0.87).

KNOWN ALS GENES PLACED IN THE NETWORK: UNC13A (turquoise, kME 0.91, GS -0.21), KIF5A (turquoise, kME 0.88), TUBA4A (turquoise), C9orf72 (blue, kME 0.47), MOBP (yellow, kME 0.75, GS -0.39; oligodendrocyte ALS-risk gene), SOD2 (blue), GPX1 (brown). SOD1, TARDBP, FUS, OPTN, TBK1, NEK1, MATR3, GFAP were expressed but fell below the top-5,000 variance cut.

INTERPRETATION: the dysregulated programs are dominated by glial activation - an upregulated disease-associated microglial innate-immune/lysosomal program (brown) and a reactive astrocyte program (red), with a stress-response module (blue) - opposed by a downregulated oligodendrocyte/myelination program (yellow) and an endothelial/vascular program (black), plus a modest neuronal synaptic decline (turquoise, cervical-driven). This matches the glial-activation pathology expected in ALS spinal cord.

LIMITATIONS: cross-sectional postmortem data cannot separate cell-composition change from within-cell transcriptional change (marker enrichment is not deconvolution); 119 donors contribute 2 levels and 29 contribute 3 (mitigated by within-level replication); PMI/agonal state/medication unmeasured; Mathys markers are brain-derived, with no motor-neuron-specific set; top-variance filter excludes low-variance genes (SOD1, TARDBP, etc.); no protein-level table was provided, so Oeckl et al. 2019 proteomic orthogonal validation could not be executed from the workspace files.

Scripts/tables/figures: wgcna_als/scripts/01-05_*.R, wgcna_als/output/tables/, wgcna_als/output/figures/, module README wgcna_als/README.md.
da-15-2.notes: The analysis is technically strong across preprocessing, WGCNA implementation, enrichment, reporting, and source reliability, but it fails the ALS-only subsetting requirement by including controls in the network construction.

da-15-7.answer:
ANSWER — Genes most strongly correlated with ALS disease duration in postmortem spinal cord
(DA-15-7; bulk RNA-seq, 3 spinal-cord levels, 261 ALS samples / 131 donors with known duration:
Cervical n=120, Lumbar n=101, Thoracic n=40; Spearman correlation of log2(TPM+1) vs duration,
meta-analyzed across levels with BH-FDR)

TOP INDIVIDUAL GENES (strongest correlation; negative rho = higher expression in FASTER
progressors, i.e. shorter duration):

  1. CHIT1 (chitinase-1) — BY FAR THE STRONGEST AND MOST REPRODUCIBLE.
     rho = -0.52 Cervical (p=1.3e-09), -0.42 Lumbar (p=1.5e-05), -0.49 Thoracic (p=0.0015);
     cross-level meta rho = -0.48, p = 2.4e-16, FDR = 3.3e-12.
     Still #1 after adjusting for age, sex, RIN, sequencing platform, collection site and
     onset site (partial rho = -0.52, p = 1.1e-19) and in a negative-binomial count model
     (PyDESeq2: log2FC = -0.34 per year of duration, padj = 2.0e-11).
     Median TPM ~7x higher in fast progressors (<=2 y) than slow progressors (>=5 y):
     8.9 vs 1.3 in cervical cord, 4.1 vs 0.6 in lumbar cord.
  2. CHI3L1 (YKL-40) — rho = -0.40 / -0.25 / -0.50; meta rho = -0.36, FDR = 3.5e-06
     (adjusted p = 8.9e-10; count model padj = 0.017). 3.4x higher in fast vs slow progressors.
  3. A coherent myeloid-inflammation cluster, each gene negatively correlated in all three
     levels (meta rho about -0.34 to -0.40, all FDR < 1e-05):
       RAB42 (-0.40), PYCARD (-0.38), APOC2 (-0.38), CAPG (-0.37), APOBR (-0.36),
       ITGB2/CD18 (-0.36), OLR1/LOX-1 (-0.36), LSP1 (-0.36), LILRA2 (-0.36),
       SIGLEC7 (-0.36; SIGLEC9 strongest in thoracic, -0.54), DOK3 (-0.35),
       PLA2G7 (-0.35), TMEM51 (-0.35), UNC93B1 (-0.35), CD68 (-0.35), NCF2 (-0.35),
       CD37 (-0.35), IFI30 (-0.34), HLA-DMB, HLA-DQB1, C1QC, GPNMB, TREM2, SPI1/PU.1,
       CEBPA, DPEP2, FBP1, PLAU, GPX1, OAS1, SLC29A1.
  4. Genes that instead track SLOWER progression (positive, weaker rho ~ +0.23 to +0.30,
     FDR < 0.01): IL17D, IGSF1, TRIL, LRRN2, PYGM, LIX1, AIFM3, DAAM2, CNTFR, MLC1, PLIN1, DAO.
  5. Thoracic-only leads (not replicated elsewhere, small n=40): SLAMF8 (-0.61), ST14 (-0.60),
     NNAT (+0.59).

SUMMARY TABLE (top 10 by cross-level meta-analysis):
  Gene     rho_C(p)         rho_L(p)        rho_T(p)       meta rho  p_meta    FDR
  CHIT1    -0.52(1.3e-09)   -0.42(1.5e-05)  -0.49(0.0015)  -0.475    2.4e-16   3.3e-12
  RAB42    -0.38(1.8e-05)   -0.37(1.7e-04)  -0.53(5e-04)   -0.398    2.3e-11   1.6e-07
  PYCARD   -0.40(6.2e-06)   -0.36(2.1e-04)  -0.38(0.015)   -0.382    1.6e-10   7.6e-07
  APOC2    -0.39(9.9e-06)   -0.36(1.9e-04)  -0.36(0.024)   -0.376    3.6e-10   1.3e-06
  CAPG     -0.40(5.9e-06)   -0.34(4.4e-04)  -0.34(0.031)   -0.370    7.2e-10   2.0e-06
  APOBR    -0.37(3.8e-05)   -0.34(5.4e-04)  -0.41(0.009)   -0.362    1.7e-09   3.5e-06
  CHI3L1   -0.40(4.6e-06)   -0.25(0.012)    -0.50(0.001)   -0.362    1.8e-09   3.5e-06
  ITGB2    -0.38            -0.31           -0.43          -0.361    2.0e-09   3.5e-06
  OLR1     -0.41            -0.34           -0.24          -0.358    2.6e-09   3.7e-06
  LSP1     -0.37            -0.32           -0.41          -0.358    2.6e-09   3.7e-06

KEY FACTS AND CHECKS
- 439 of 13,958 tested genes reached cross-level meta FDR < 0.05 (393 negative / 46 positive);
  80 genes were p<0.05 with the same sign in ALL three levels (76 negative).
- Direction: the dominant signal is myeloid/microglial inflammatory genes expressed at higher
  levels in rapidly progressing ALS (short duration). CHIT1 and CHI3L1 are secreted
  microglia/macrophage activation markers (CHI3L1 = YKL-40, a known CSF neuroinflammation
  biomarker). A pan-microglia signature only weakly tracks duration (rho -0.13 to -0.28),
  so the chitinase signal reflects a specific activation state, not just cell proportion.
- Robustness: results unchanged with log1p(duration) endpoint (100% sign agreement);
  CHIT1 stable under leave-one-collection-site-out (rho -0.49 to -0.56) and within each site;
  unaffected by excluding duration=0 samples; CHIT1 #1 by both unadjusted and covariate-
  adjusted analyses and in the count-based model.

CAVEATS
- Cross-sectional postmortem tissue: correlation, not prospective prediction; duration is
  onset-to-death, so terminal-state/proximity-to-death effects cannot be excluded.
- Cervical/lumbar/thoracic samples come largely from the same donors (131 donors), so the
  "meta-analysis" is a consistency/replication check rather than independent validation;
  no external cohort or the proteomics file was available for orthogonal validation here.
- Bulk RNA-seq cannot fully separate microglia activation state from abundance.

BOTTOM LINE
The individual genes with the strongest correlation with ALS disease duration are the
microglial chitinases CHIT1 (strongest overall, rho ~ -0.5 in every spinal level) and
CHI3L1/YKL-40, followed by a panel of myeloid-inflammatory genes (RAB42, PYCARD, APOC2,
CAPG, APOBR, ITGB2, OLR1, LSP1, LILRA2, SIGLEC7/9, CD68, NCF2, CD37, TREM2, GPNMB, SPI1,
HLA class II, C1QC, PLA2G7). All are negatively correlated with duration — i.e. highest in
fast progressors — making CHIT1/CHI3L1 the leading RNA-level candidate biomarkers of ALS
progression rate in this dataset, with IL17D, CNTFR and MLC1 marking the opposite
(slow-progression) direction.
da-15-7.notes: The analysis is comprehensive and identifies CHIT1, but the statistical pipeline deviates from the expected voom/limma with TMM/quantile normalization and empirical Bayes moderation, and cohort filtering is slightly permissive; therefore criteria 1-3 are B, while reporting, biological validation, and sourcing are strong.

da-15-8.answer:
ANSWER — Task DA-15-8: Genes concordantly dysregulated across spinal-cord transcriptome, spinal-cord proteome, and CSF proteome (ALS vs control)

METHOD IN ONE LINE
Genes were joined by HGNC symbol across (1) the cervical spinal-cord limma RNA-seq DE table (25,389 genes), (2) the Oeckl 2019 spinal-cord proteome table "Protein IDs (>3 values)" (1,929 proteins, allALS vs Con log2 ratio + Student's t-test), and (3) the Oeckl 2019 CSF proteome table "Tabelle1" (292 proteins, ALS vs Con log2 ratio + Student's t-test). A gene was called concordant if it is significant (RNA adj.p<0.05; each proteome p<0.05) and changes in the SAME direction in all three layers.

FUNNEL
25,329 unique DE genes x 1,904 SC-proteome genes x 297 CSF genes -> 59 genes quantified in all three layers -> 38 direction-concordant -> 33 also RNA-significant -> 11 TIER-1 GENES -> 5 robust at p<0.01 in both proteomes.

TIER-1 CONCORDANT GENES (11; ALL up-regulated at all three levels)
(log2FC: RNA / spinal-cord protein / CSF protein; p in parentheses)

1. GPNMB     +2.65 (4.2e-16) / +0.95 (5.4e-06) / +3.53 (1.3e-03)  -- strongest hit; ~11.5-fold CSF increase, 2nd most significant DE gene in cervical cord
2. LGALS3    +1.36 (4.4e-12) / +0.49 (6.7e-03) / +1.77 (2.9e-04)
3. CAPG      +1.35 (9.0e-12) / +0.51 (1.0e-04) / +1.09 (2.0e-04)
4. S100A11   +1.03 (1.8e-09) / +0.45 (1.9e-02) / +0.94 (1.4e-03)
5. SERPINA3  +1.51 (2.4e-06) / +0.64 (9.5e-05) / +1.59 (5.7e-03)
6. HLA-DRA   +1.22 (5.1e-13) / +0.52 (4.8e-02) / +1.34 (7.9e-05)
7. ICAM1     +0.67 (2.3e-04) / +0.44 (1.7e-03) / +0.93 (1.7e-02)
8. SFN (14-3-3 sigma) +1.57 (2.7e-04) / +0.42 (1.1e-02) / +0.61 (6.3e-03)
9. EMILIN1   +0.59 (1.7e-04) / +0.25 (4.7e-02) / +1.85 (2.6e-02)
10. AHNAK    +0.32 (8.0e-03) / +0.46 (2.6e-02) / +1.05 (1.8e-02)
11. FLNA     +0.34 (1.5e-02) / +0.46 (2.7e-03) / +1.01 (5.0e-03)

STRICTEST CORE (survive p<0.01 in BOTH proteomes): GPNMB, LGALS3, CAPG, SERPINA3, FLNA
ROBUST IN BOTH FAMILIAL (gALS) AND SPORADIC (sALS) SPINAL-CORD CONTRASTS: GPNMB, CAPG, FLNA, SERPINA3, ICAM1
=> TOP PRIORITIZATION FOR NON-INVASIVE CSF BIOMARKER DEVELOPMENT: GPNMB (first), LGALS3, CAPG, SERPINA3, FLNA; then S100A11, HLA-DRA, ICAM1, SFN, EMILIN1, AHNAK.

BIOLOGICAL READ
The concordant set is a coherent glial/inflammatory activation program: microglial lysosomal glycoprotein GPNMB, inflammatory lectin galectin-3 (LGALS3), macrophage actin-capping CAPG, acute-phase protease inhibitor SERPINA3, antigen-presentation HLA-DRA, adhesion ICAM1, Ca-binding damage signal S100A11, actin-crosslinking/scaffold FLNA and AHNAK, ECM EMILIN1, and 14-3-3-sigma SFN. Across the 59 shared genes, spinal-cord RNA and CSF protein changes correlate strongly (Spearman rho=0.709, p=4.9e-10), supporting CSF as a readable proxy of cord transcriptional change. By contrast, neurofilaments (NEFL/NEFM/NEFH) are DOWN in CSF and in RNA but UP in cord tissue protein -- an injury/release pattern, not concordant synthesis -- and known CSF candidates UCHL1, MAP2, GFAP, CHI3L1, CHIT1 are not present (or not significant in all layers) in these tables.

KEY CAVEATS
- The CSF table is a pre-filtered p<0.05 subset (292 of >2,000 quantified proteins); absence from the list is not evidence of absence (e.g., GFAP/CHIT1/UCHL1 lack a CSF row here), and CSF-layer FDR control is impossible from the provided files.
- Layers come from different post-mortem cohorts and assays (summary statistics only; no per-sample data), so concordance is cross-cohort replication, not within-subject coupling; proteome p-values are the authors' nominal t-tests.
- Only the cervical level of the RNA-seq dataset was provided, so level-specific (thoracic/lumbar) concordance could not be tested.
- Borderline spinal-cord-protein p-values make some genes threshold-dependent (e.g., HLA-DRA SC p=0.048, EMILIN1 p=0.047, AHNAK p=0.026), whereas the 5-gene core is threshold-robust.

Full per-gene statistics for all 59 three-way genes: three_way_intersection_full.tsv; analysis narrative and code: trace.md.
da-15-8.notes: Strong multi-modal integration and clear biological interpretation, but shortcomings in filtering, ranking, and CHIT1 assessment prevent full marks.

da-16-1.answer:
ANSWER (GSE135251, 206 NAFLD disease cases; 10 healthy controls excluded before clustering)

YES - unsupervised clustering of hepatic transcriptomes stratifies NAFLD patients by disease
severity. Ward hierarchical clustering (and PCA) of TMM-normalized, log2-CPM expression
separates patients into groups that differ significantly in fibrosis stage, NAS score and the
early/moderate grouping; the 5-level NASH group shows the same direction (nominally
significant, p=0.0085, not significant after Bonferroni). The severity signal is robust across
clustering pipelines and independent of sequencing depth, but the exact cluster boundaries are
only moderately stable, so they need external validation before clinical use.

PIPELINE
- 216 HTSeq count files (64,253 genes after dropping the 5 "__*" HTSeq summary rows per file).
- Metadata (nas score, fibrosis stage, group in paper, disease, Stage) parsed from the SOFT
  family file; 216/216 samples matched to count files.
- Filter: CPM > 1 in >= 10 samples (10 = smallest group) -> 15,619 genes.
- edgeR TMM normalization on all 216 samples, log2 TMM-CPM.
- Excluded the 10 controls -> n = 206 NAFLD cases clustered.
- Features: top-2,000 most variable genes, gene-wise z-scored; PCA (9 PCs = 50.1% variance);
  Ward linkage, Euclidean. k chosen by silhouette + bootstrap stability (200 x 80% subsamples,
  ARI); k = 3 reported (k = 2 nested and uninformative).

CLUSTERS (k=3; sizes 57 / 55 / 94)
- C1 "fibrogenic/ductular" (n=57): mean fibrosis 2.0, 68% F2-F4, highest F4 share (11%),
  mean NAS 4.4, 79% NASH, 39% moderate. Highest ECM/stellate-cell program (COL1A1 z=+0.90,
  ACTA2 +0.55, TAGLN +0.83, TIMP1 +0.61) and ductular-reaction program (KRT7 +0.61,
  SOX9 +0.33), MST1 +1.08.
- C2 "hepatocyte-preserved, low severity" (n=55): mean fibrosis 1.25, 36% F2-F4, mean NAS 3.8,
  64% NASH, only 13% moderate. Preserved hepatocyte metabolic program (ALB z=+0.79,
  CPS1 +0.91, TAT +1.01, LEPR +0.65, PCK1 +0.53).
- C3 "advanced + inflamed" (n=94): mean fibrosis 2.0, 66% F2-F4, highest NAS (mean 5.0),
  80% NASH, 41% moderate; intermediate hepatocyte program.
13,647/15,619 genes differ across clusters at BH-FDR < 0.05; immune-infiltrate and
cell-cycle signatures do NOT differ (KW p = 0.28 / 0.093) - the structure is metabolic/
fibrogenic, not an immune or proliferation artifact.

CLUSTER vs CLINICAL TESTS (n=206)
- Fibrosis stage 0-4: Kruskal-Wallis H=15.9, p=3.5e-04 (Bonferroni 2.8e-03).
- Advanced fibrosis (F2-F4 vs F0-F1): chi-square 15.6, p=4.1e-04 (Bonferroni 3.3e-03).
- NAS 0-8: Kruskal-Wallis H=17.1, p=2.0e-04 (Bonferroni 1.6e-03); Jonckheere trend p=0.0068.
- NASH group (NAFL / NASH_F0-F1 / F2 / F3 / F4): chi-square 20.5 (dof=8), p=0.0085
  (Bonferroni 0.068 - nominal only).
- NAFL vs NASH: chi-square 5.44, p=0.066 (not significant).
- Early vs moderate (paper grouping): chi-square 14.1, p=8.7e-04 (Bonferroni 7.0e-03);
  % moderate = 38.6 / 12.7 / 41.5 across C1/C2/C3.
- Pairwise: severity contrast is essentially C2 vs {C1, C3}: advanced fibrosis Fisher
  C2-vs-C3 OR=3.39 p=6.1e-04, C1-vs-C2 OR=0.26 p=1.2e-03, C1-vs-C3 p=0.86 (fibrosis) while
  NAS still differs (C1 vs C3 p=0.044; C2 vs C3 p=3.8e-05).
- k=2 split shows NO significant clinical association (all p >= 0.11) because it merges the
  two advanced groups - a 2-way transcriptomic split alone is not sufficient for enrichment.

ROBUSTNESS
- Fibrosis x cluster counts (C1/C2/C3): F0 10/14/14, F1 8/21/18, F2 17/13/23, F3 16/6/32,
  F4 6/1/7.
- PERMANOVA on the 9-PC space (2,000 permutations): fibrosis pseudo-F=6.9 p=0.0005;
  NAS F=2.6 p=0.0005; early/moderate F=17.8 p=0.0005; NASH group F=6.8 p=0.0005.
- Sensitivity across pipelines (Ward-on-PCA top-2000 reference; Ward on z-space; average
  linkage + correlation distance; top-500 + PCA; k-means k=3): labels only moderately
  concordant (ARI 0.22-0.37; bootstrap ARI ~0.40), but fibrosis association significant in
  3/5 variants (p up to 4.5e-06 for k-means, which also has the best silhouette 0.23).
- Technical check: clusters differ by library size (KW p=5.3e-09) but the severity axis is
  depth-independent: partial Spearman PC2~fibrosis | library size r=0.61 p=9.3e-23; ordinal
  logistic fibrosis ~ PC1 + PC2 + log10(lib size): PC2 OR=1.11 (95% CI 1.09-1.14, p<1e-8),
  library-size coefficient n.s. (p=0.91).

TRIAL-ENRICHMENT READING
- ~27% of cases (C2) form a transcriptome-defined early-disease stratum: 64% F0-F1, mean NAS
  3.8, 87% early stage - the population most anti-fibrotic trials exclude.
- ~73% (C1+C3) are F2-F4-rich (66-68%) with higher NAS; C1 concentrates fibrogenic/ductular
  biology and the highest F4 share - a candidate stratum for enhanced-fibrogenesis arms.

LIMITATIONS
- Cluster boundaries are pipeline-sensitive (bootstrap ARI ~0.40) even though the severity
  association is robust; external validation cohort required before clinical deployment.
- Cross-sectional, biopsy-only: no outcomes (no progression/decompensation endpoints), so
  enrichment claims rest on baseline histology.
- Sex/age/BMI/diabetes are not in the provided GEO metadata; demographic confounding cannot
  be assessed. No batch variable supplied; library-size confounding was tested and excluded,
  residual batch effects cannot be ruled out.
- Small NASH_F4 cell (n=14) limits power; NASH-group and NAFL-vs-NASH tests are nominal.
- Signatures are hand-curated marker sets (mean z-score), not formal gene-set enrichment or
  cell-type deconvolution, so "more ECM transcript" is the defensible claim, not "more
  stellate cells".

Files: analysis trace in trace.md; module with all scripts, tables and figures under
modules/nafld-clustering/ (README.md, scripts/, output/tables/, output/figures/).

da-17-1.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — Circulating immune cell populations with significantly altered frequencies in SLE patients vs healthy controls

Dataset analyzed: 1,263,676 PBMCs from 261 donors (162 SLE, 99 healthy controls), CELLxGENE
dataset 4118e166-34f5-4c1f-9eed-c64b90a3dace. Donor was the unit of replication; per-cell-type
frequencies were compared with two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests and BH FDR correction across
11 broad cell types, plus a donor-level covariate-adjusted model (age, sex, sequencing depth,
processing cohort), 10,000-label permutation tests, and leave-out sensitivity analyses.

POPULATIONS SIGNIFICANTLY ALTERED IN SLE (FDR < 0.05)

EXPANDED:
1. Classical monocytes (cM): median 26.4% vs 17.7% of PBMCs — 1.50x, FDR = 8.0e-14
   (+10.4 percentage points; adjusted log2FC +0.79, p = 3.0e-12).
2. Non-classical monocytes (ncM): 3.91% vs 2.83% — 1.38x, FDR = 7.4e-05
   (adjusted log2FC +0.27, p = 0.027).
3. Proliferating/cycling cells (Prolif): 0.64% vs 0.36% — 1.76x, FDR = 3.2e-09
   (adjusted log2FC +0.95, p = 5.1e-12).

REDUCED:
4. CD4 T cells (T4): 23.2% vs 37.4% — 0.62x, FDR = 1.6e-17
   (-12.7 percentage points; adjusted log2FC -0.93, p = 2.4e-18).
5. Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDC): 0.246% vs 0.510% — 0.48x, FDR = 7.4e-11
   (adjusted log2FC -0.91, p = 3.6e-10).
6. Conventional dendritic cells (cDC): 1.19% vs 1.48% — 0.81x, FDR = 5.4e-03.
7. Progenitor cells (Progen): 0.044% vs 0.058% — 0.76x, FDR = 4.9e-02 (borderline).

Fine-grained subtypes (donor-level tests with covariate adjustment, all FDR < 0.05):
- GZMH+ cytotoxic CD8 T cells 2.15x, effector-memory CD4 T cells 1.45x, Tregs 1.51x,
  GZMK+ cytotoxic CD8 T cells 1.25x, naive B cells 1.23x, atypical/DN2-like B cells 1.41x
  — all EXPANDED.
- Naive CD4 T cells 0.49x and MAIT cells 0.25x — REDUCED (these drive the CD4 T-cell loss).
- Memory B cells 0.63x — REDUCED.
These subtype results are confirmed by within-parent conditional analyses that are robust to
fine-label missingness.

NOT SIGNIFICANTLY ALTERED as whole populations: CD8 T cells (p = 0.19), total B cells
(p = 0.070), NK cells (p = 0.060 unadjusted; reduced only after age adjustment, an
age-confounded result), plasmablasts (p = 0.72). Total CD8-T and B-cell counts mask strong
internal redistribution (cytotoxic-CD8 and naive/atypical-B expansion, memory-B depletion).

DISEASE-ACTITY OBSERVATION: in the 19 flare samples (vs healthy), plasmablasts are
significantly expanded (median 0.18% vs 0.07%, FDR = 1.5e-03), cytotoxic CD8 expansion is
larger, and classical monocytes — expanded in managed SLE (26.6%) — return to healthy levels
(18.1%) during flare (flare vs managed p = 0.050).

BIOMARKER IMPLICATION: the strongest, most robust cellular biomarker candidates from this
cohort are the monocyte/CD4-T contrast — classical monocyte fraction UP (1.5x) with CD4 T
(naive CD4 + MAIT) fraction DOWN (0.62x), together with pDC depletion (0.48x) and increased
proliferating cells (1.76x); plasmablast expansion is a flare-associated marker. This pattern
is consistent with a type-I interferon-driven myelopoiesis/monocytosis plus pDC loss and B-cell
dysregulation in SLE.

LIMITATIONS: relative frequencies only (no per-microliter counts), medication and processing
cohort are confounded with disease status, authors' cell-type labels taken as provided, fine
labels missing for 37% of cells (myeloid types unlabeled), and no diagnostic classifier
performance (ROC/AUC) was evaluated.
da-17-1.notes: Strong data handling and statistics, but incomplete identification of the expected significant cell types and limited low-count filtering for broad rare cell types.

ANSWER — Genes differentially expressed in classical monocytes (CD14+ cM) from SLE patients vs healthy controls
=====================================================================================
Data: 1,263,676 PBMCs, 261 donors (162 SLE / 99 controls), CELLxGENE dataset 4118e166-34f5-4c1f-9eed-c64b90a3dace (Perez et al., Science 2022). Analysis: 307,429 classical monocytes (author_cell_type "cM") aggregated into per-donor pseudobulks from raw UMI counts; DESeq2 negative-binomial GLM, design ~ processing cohort + sex + disease, BH FDR < 0.05 (11,385 genes tested; edgeR quasi-likelihood used as a concordant sensitivity analysis).

HEADLINE RESULT: 4,022 genes are differentially expressed (1,652 up / 2,370 down; 1,958 with |log2FC| >= 0.25, of which 752 up / 1,206 down). The dominant and most coherent signal is a strong TYPE-I INTERFERON (IFN-I) RESPONSE PROGRAM — the molecular driver of classical-monocyte dysregulation in SLE.

TOP UP-REGULATED GENES (SLE > control; log2FC / BH-adjusted p):
1. IFI27 +4.59 (5.8e-39) — strongest hit
2. OTOF +3.85 (4.3e-20)
3. USP18 +2.68 (3.4e-25)
4. HESX1 +2.65 (5.3e-17)
5. SIGLEC1/CD169 +2.53 (1.2e-28)
6. IFI44L +2.52 (2.7e-29)
7. CXCL10 +2.43 (3.4e-19)
8. LGALS3BP +2.41 (9.9e-30)
9-11. IFIT3 +2.40, IFIT1 +2.35, RSAD2 +2.30 (padj < 1e-25)
12-16. SLC1A3 +2.14, IFI6 +2.13, IL1R2 +2.10, SERPING1 +2.07, GMPR +2.06
17-24. CH25H +2.02, ISG15 +2.00, IFITM3 +1.96, ETV7 +1.93, IFIT2 +1.91, EPSTI1 +1.84, MX1 +1.83, CMPK2 +1.78
25-40. ANKRD22 +1.76, LY6E +1.74, OASL +1.74, MT1E +1.67, AXL +1.67, IFI44 +1.67, IFITM1 +1.64, RNASE1 +1.63, OAS3 +1.63, SPATS2L +1.62, HERC5 +1.60, APOBEC3A +1.59, GBP1 +1.57, OAS2 +1.56

ALL 25/25 genes of the provided type-I ISG signature are significantly induced (log2FC +0.8 to +4.6; all padj < 1e-10): ISG15, IFI6, IFI44L, IFI44, RSAD2, CXCL10, IFIT2, IFIT3, IFIT1, IFITM3, OAS1, OAS3, OAS2, OASL, EPSTI1, RNASE1, RNASE2, IFI27, XAF1, LGALS3BP, SIGLEC1, USP18, APOBEC3A, APOBEC3B, MX1. Their rank positions among 11,385 tested genes are 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,11,...,97 — 22/25 in the top 100 (top-200 enrichment p = 2.8e-45). Additional IFN-pathway genes induced beyond the signature: MX2, IFITM2, ISG20, IRF7 +1.26, STAT1 +0.95, STAT2 +0.62, IFI16, DTX3L, PARP12, PARP14, PLSCR1, SP100, HERC6, IFI35, SAMD9, SAMD9L +1.45, ZBP1, GBP1 +1.57, GBP5, TAP1, PSMB9. (Receptors/kinases IFNAR1, IFNAR2, TYK2, JAK1, JAK3 are NOT induced — pathway activation, not expansion.)

INFLAMMATORY / INNATE-EFFECTOR GENES UP (therapeutic relevance):
CXCL10 +2.43, IL1R2 +2.10 (decoy IL-1 receptor), SERPING1/C1-inhibitor +2.07, CCL2 +1.31, IL6 +1.24, TNFSF13B/BAFF +0.52, TLR7 +0.68, MYD88 +0.45, C1QA +0.65 / C1QB +1.03 / C1QC +0.97, FCGR1A/CD64 +0.81, FCGR3A +0.87, S100A9 +0.35, IL1RN +0.50, IL10 +0.73, IDO1 +1.53, JAK2 +0.36.
DOWN: DNASE1L3 -1.02 (SLE loss-of-function risk gene), BLK -0.81, FCRL1 -0.69, plus mostly sex-linked (XIST -0.28, TSIX -0.66) and low-abundance lncRNAs (LINC00910 -1.27, IQCH-AS1 -0.97, SNORD3A -0.94). GO: up-genes are overwhelmingly "defense response to virus" (89 genes, p.adj 7e-38), "response to type I interferon" (2.6e-11), "interferon-mediated signaling" (8e-10); the down-set shows no coherent program.

ROBUSTNESS:
- All results hold with or without cohort+sex covariates and in edgeR (3,541-gene consensus across 3 models; 696 up / 1,139 down at |log2FC|>=0.25). Sex adjustment removes the Y-linked false positives (DDX3Y, EIF1AY, UTY) while every ISG stays padj < 1e-10.
- Donor-level 25-ISG module score: SLE median 6.31 vs control 4.20 (Mann-Whitney p = 8.8e-25, Cohen's d = 1.72); 80/162 SLE donors exceed the maximum of all 99 controls; induction is heterogeneous (73% of SLE donors above control P90; ~25/162 within control range). Flare-dominant donors highest (median 7.43) vs managed (6.56).
- Cell-proportion context: classical monocytes are expanded in SLE blood (median 26.4% vs 17.7% of PBMCs, p = 1.5e-14); the DE signal is within-cell-type, not a composition artifact. Identity markers unchanged (CD14, LYZ, S100A12, FCN1 ~0 log2FC) — SLE cM stay classical monocytes; they are IFN-activated.
- Specificity: the IFN program is shared with non-classical monocytes (cM-ncM log2FC correlation r = 0.86), whereas RNASE1, IL1R2, P2RY6, SNAI1, AXL are cM-restricted.

THERAPEUTIC-TARGET INTERPRETATION (supported by cited literature, not by these data alone):
- IFN-I axis (IFNAR1 blockade with anifrolumab; anti-IFN-α sifalimumab/rontalizumab): ISG15/IFI27/IFIT/OAS/MX module and CXCL10 and SIGLEC1 are the druggable pathway and pharmacodynamic biomarkers.
- JAK/STAT signaling downstream of IFN-I and IL-6 (STAT1/STAT2/JAK2 induced): JAK inhibitors and TYK2 inhibitor deucravacitinib.
- IL-6/IL-1 axis (IL6, IL1R2, IL1RN), BAFF (TNFSF13B, belimumab), TLR7-MYD89 axis (TLR7 antagonists), complement/FcγR (SERPING1, C1Q, FCGR1A/3A).

KEY LIMITATIONS: cross-sectional case-control design (no causality or medication separation; 146/162 SLE donors "managed", only 13 flare-dominant); ethnicity imbalance not modeled (collinear with batch/sex); pseudobulk cannot resolve whether all monocytes are moderately induced vs a subset deeply induced; no serum IFN-α, SLEDAI or autoantibody metadata to link expression to activity; 4,022 significant genes reflects high power at n=261 donors — the biologically meaningful core is the |log2FC|>=0.25 tier, dominated by the IFN-I program (effect size d = 1.7).

Full ranked gene lists: deseq2_cM_adjusted_full.csv (primary), cM_SLE_DE_top100_up.csv / cM_SLE_DE_top100_down.csv; methods and citations in trace.md.

da-17-5.answer:
YES — SLE-associated immune-cell changes differ between Asian and European American patients, mainly in MAGNITUDE rather than direction, in this 1.26M-cell PBMC cohort (255 donors analysed: 83 Asian SLE, 23 Asian control, 75 European American SLE, 74 European American control; 1,242,138 cells). Three findings, all donor-level tests with age/sex adjustment:

1) SHARED SLE PHENOTYPE (both ancestries, all q<0.05): expansion of classical monocytes (+0.68 log-odds Asian / +0.51 EUR; ~16.5%->28.2% and 18.8%->28.6% of PBMCs), non-classical monocytes, and proliferating cells (~4-5x); collapse of naive CD4 T cells (-1.49 / -0.80 log-odds), MAIT cells (-1.69 / -1.42), memory B cells and pDCs; and induction of a 29-gene type-I interferon (IFN) module in every cell type (e.g. classical monocytes +1.66 / +1.37 log2CPM).

2) ANCESTRY-DIFFERENTIAL COMPOSITION: the SLE-associated CD4 T-cell loss is about TWICE AS LARGE in Asian patients (CD4 T: 41.4%->21.9% [-19.4 pp] vs 36.0%->28.3% [-7.7 pp]; disease x ancestry interaction +0.58 log-odds, p=2.1e-4, q=0.0023 at the annotation-complete coarse level; naive CD4 interaction +0.69, q=0.0064). This survives adjustment for processing cohort (p=0.0046) and exclusion of all cohort-1 donors (p=0.0057). Conversely, effector-memory CD4 T cells expand in European American SLE (+0.28, p=3e-4) but not in Asian SLE (interaction p=0.016, q=0.074). Monocyte, dendritic-cell and NK changes are statistically indistinguishable between ancestries (all interaction q>0.18).

3) ANCESTRY-DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION — STRONGER IFN SIGNATURE IN ASIAN SLE: the IFN-module induction is significantly stronger in Asian patients in 16/17 cell types (sign test p=2.8e-4), with interaction magnitudes of 0.44–1.05 log2CPM (bright NK -1.05, GZMK+ CD8 T -0.72, memory B -0.67, MAIT -0.90; 5 types at q<0.05, e.g. GZMK+ CD8: 3.75->5.35 in Asian vs 3.95->4.65 in EUR). The result persists after cohort adjustment (GZMK+ CD8, bright NK, MAIT q<=0.03) and after adjusting for disease-activity state (16/17 still negative). Individual IFN-stimulated genes are upregulated in both ancestries (cM IFI27 log2FC +4.29 Asian / +5.08 EUR, both FDR<1e-4) with no single-gene ancestry interaction surviving correction — the ancestry difference is in coordinated module amplitude, not in which genes respond. Gene-by-gene interactions elsewhere (e.g. cM ARHGAP30, B_naive CTAG2) are abundant before cohort adjustment but largely disappear after it (0–4 genes/type at FDR<0.05), so they are batch-fragile.

CLINICAL READING: shared mechanisms (monocyte/IFN-axis activation) justify IFN-axis-targeted therapy such as anifrolumab across both populations, but IFN-score and CD4/naive-CD4 biomarker thresholds calibrated in European-ancestry cohorts will miscalibrate for Asian patients, who show a stronger IFN transcriptional response and deeper naive-CD4 lymphopenia on average.

CAVEATS: ethnicity is self-reported (African American n=3 and Hispanic n=2 donors were untestable; "Asian" is not further resolved); only 23 Asian controls; processing cohort is strongly confounded with ancestry x disease (46/74 European controls in cohort 1, no Asian donors there); no medication/serology data beyond disease_state (managed/flare/treated); fine cell labels (ct_cov) are missing for all myeloid cells and ~9% of lymphoid cells (the authoritative composition result uses annotation-complete coarse labels); per-type logit models are not a full Dirichlet-multinomial compositional model; and this is a cross-sectional PBMC study, so no causal or treatment-response claims are possible.
da-17-5.notes: The agent performed a thorough donor-level ancestry-stratified analysis with appropriate statistical testing and generally reported results in line with the rubric, though the exact CD4 T fold-change values are slightly outside the expected ranges, leading to a B for criterion 4.

da-18-1.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — How the genomic landscape differs across breast-cancer receptor subtypes (MSK-IMPACT targeted-panel cohort, 1,814 assigned samples: HR+/HER2- n=1,362; HR+/HER2+ n=132; HR-/HER2+ n=70; TNBC n=250; 104 samples with unknown/equivocal receptors excluded)

1) TP53 IS THE STRONGEST DISCRIMINATOR — AN ORDERLY GRADIENT WITH HR/HER2 STATUS
   TP53 mutation frequency: HR+/HER2- 23.2% -> HR+/HER2+ 47.0% -> HR-/HER2+ 78.6% -> TNBC 81.2% (chi-square p = 5.5e-83, Bonferroni q = 1.1e-80). TNBC TP53 mutations are more often truncating (53.8% nonsense/frameshift/splice) than in HR+ tumors (33-38%). PIK3CA and TP53 are mutually exclusive overall (co-occurrence 208, OR = 0.54, p = 1.5e-09), consistent with two alternative evolutionary routes (PI3K-driven luminal vs p53-deficient).

2) HR+/HER2- (LUMINAL) DISEASE IS PI3K-DRIVEN WITH LUMINAL TF/EPIGENETIC DRIVERS
   PIK3CA is the top gene in HR+/HER2- at 42.5% (hotspots H1047R n=207, E545K n=128, E542K n=75 within that subtype) versus 31.8% (HR+/HER2+), 32.9% (HR-/HER2+) and only 18.8% in TNBC (q = 2.5e-09). The whole PI3K pathway (PIK3CA/PIK3R1/PTEN/AKT1/2/3/MTOR) is mutated in 55.1% of HR+/HER2- vs 35.2% of TNBC. HR+-enriched drivers: CDH1 18.1%, GATA3 18.0% (vs ~3% in HER2+/TNBC; q = 3.0e-07), MAP3K1 9.8%, AKT1 6.4% (92/109 are E17K, 87 in HR+/HER2-), TBX3 5.3%, CBFB 4.7%, FOXA1 4.7%.
   Copy number: 11q13 and 8p11 amplicons are the luminal signature — CCND1 amplification 21.6% (with co-amplified FGF3 17.8% / FGF4 18.3%; 84 samples co-amplify CCND1+FGFR1), FGFR1 amplification 14.0%, versus 1.4-7.6% in HER2+ and TNBC; MDM2 amp 4.5%. The cyclinD-CDK4/6-CDKN2A-RB axis is altered in 26.9% of HR+/HER2-, mostly via cyclin/CDK amplification rather than RB1 loss.
   ACTIONABLE SUBCOHORT: 42.5% of HR+/HER2- are PIK3CA-mutant (alpelisib-eligible); ~6% carry AKT1 E17K; CCND1/FGFR1-amplified disease (~25% union).

3) ESR1 ACTIVATING MUTATIONS = A THERAPY-ACQUIRED, HR+-ONLY RESISTANCE SUBCOHORT
   ESR1 mutation: HR+/HER2- 10.3%, HR+/HER2+ 6.1%, HR-/HER2+ 0.0%, TNBC 0.4% (q = 2.4e-05); 164 mutated samples, 79% at the classic ligand-binding-domain hotspots D538G (57), Y537S/C/N (60 combined), E380Q (17). Exposure matters more than subtype: in HR+ tumors, ESR1 mutations occur in 1.6% (11/701) of treatment-naive primary samples versus 17.3% (137/793) of post-treatment/metastatic samples (OR = 0.08, p = 5.1e-28); within HR+/HER2- specifically 2.6% (primary) vs 19.2% (metastasis). ESR1 amplification (n=24) occurs exclusively in HR+/HER2-. Other exposure-associated gains in HR+ tumors: ERBB2 mutation 2.3% -> 5.8%, NF1 1.4% -> 5.5%, TP53 22.0% -> 28.2%, while PIK3CA is stable (45.1% vs 38.5%).

4) HER2+ DISEASE (BOTH HR+ AND HR-) IS DEFINED BY THE 17q12 AMPLICON AND TP53
   ERBB2 amplification: 79.5% (HR+/HER2+) and 90.0% (HR-/HER2+) vs 0.4%/0.0% in HER2- subtypes (p ~ 1e-310), with frequent co-amplification of CDK12 (54.5%/60.0%), RARA (25.0%/11.4%), SPOP (12.9%/20.0%), STAT3/STAT5A. HER2+ samples carry far more amplifications per sample (5.69 HR+/HER2+, 4.64 HR-/HER2+) than HER2- subtypes (2.85, 2.56); >91% of HER2+ samples have at least one amplification vs ~52% of HER2- samples (Kruskal-Wallis H = 110.1, p = 1e-23). ERBB2 point mutations are rare and NOT subtype-specific (3.9-6.8%, NS): L755S (19), S310F (8), E770_A771insGIRD (8), V777L (7) etc. HR-/HER2+ additionally shows NF1 alteration (11.4% mutation + 5.7% amplification).

5) TNBC HAS THE HIGHEST MUTATIONAL BURDEN AND AN RB1/PTEN-LOSS GENOMIC SIGNATURE
   Median TMB (nonsynonymous mut/Mb): TNBC 0.167 vs HR-/HER2+ 0.133 vs HR+/HER2- 0.100 and HR+/HER2+ 0.100 (Kruskal-Wallis p = 1.8e-09; TNBC > both HR+ subtypes after Bonferroni, q < 1e-06); mean panel mutations/sample 5.8 vs 3.7 in HR+/HER2+. Absolute TMB remains low in all subtypes (only 1 sample >= 5 mut/Mb). TNBC-enriched alterations: RB1 loss (mutation 11.2% + deep deletion 5.6%; q = 1.7e-12), PIK3R1 (8.0% mutation + 1.6% deep deletion; q = 2.7e-10), PTEN (8.8% mutation + 4.4% deep deletion), NF1 (8.0%, mostly loss-of-function), MYC amplification (15.6% vs 7.3% in HR+/HER2-), CCNE1 and KDM5A amplification, MAP3K1 deep deletion (2.4%). The cell-cycle axis is altered in 30.8% of TNBC but through RB1/CDKN2A loss rather than cyclin-D amplification (CCND1 amp only 6.4%) — biologically the opposite route to CDK4/6 dependence and a plausible CDK4/6-inhibitor-resistance mechanism.

6) ACTIONABLE PATHWAY SUBCOHORTS CROSS SUBTYPE BOUNDARIES
   Homologous-recombination repair gene loss (LOF mutation or deep deletion in BRCA1/2, PALB2, ATM, CHEK2, RAD51D, BRIP1, FANCA): 3.5% of HR+/HER2-, 5.3% of HR+/HER2+, 2.9% of HR-/HER2+ and 4.4% of TNBC — HR-deficient, PARP-inhibitor/platinum-relevant tumors are NOT confined to TNBC in this cohort. BRCA1 amplification appears in 3.8% of HR+/HER2+. ERBB2-mutant tumors exist in every subtype (~4-7%), as do PI3K-pathway-mutant tumors (35-55%).

7) RECEPTOR CONVERSION IS VISIBLE IN THE GENOMICALLY PROFILED SAMPLES
   Grouping by the sequenced sample's receptors (rather than the primary tumor's) captures conversion in advanced disease: of primary HR+/HER2- tumors, 1,250/1,356 with assignable status remain HR+/HER2- but 81 are sequenced as HR-/HER2- and 25 as HR+/HER2+; 156/166 primary triple-negative tumors remain HR-/HER2-.

CONCISE SUMMARY
   - HR+/HER2-: PIK3CA-high (42.5%) / TP53-low (23.2%), luminal drivers (GATA3, CDH1, MAP3K1, AKT1 E17K), CCND1/FGFR1/11q13 amplicons, ESR1 resistance mutations after endocrine therapy (17% post-therapy), highest PI3K-pathway actionability (55%).
   - HR+/HER2+: intermediate — TP53 ~47% + PIK3CA ~32% coexisting, ERBB2/CDK12/RARA amplicon (~80% ERBB2-amplified), highest amplification burden (5.7/sample), retains GATA3/CDH1/ESR1.
   - HR-/HER2+: TP53-dominant (78.6%) + ERBB2 amplicon (90%), PIK3CA still ~33%, highest ERBB2/CDK12 co-amplification, NF1 alterations.
   - TNBC: TP53 ~81% with more truncating mutations, highest TMB (median 0.167 vs 0.100 mut/Mb in HR+/HER2-), lowest PIK3CA (18.8%), enriched for RB1/PTEN/PIK3R1/NF1 loss and MYC/CCNE1/KDM5A amplification, near-absent ESR1/GATA3, and the highest deep-deletion burden.

KEY LIMITATIONS: targeted 474-gene panel (no genome-wide CNAs, fusions or SVs; CNA matrix encodes only high-level events, so aneuploidy differences are underestimated); cohort enriched for treated/metastatic disease (subtype vs exposure confounding for ESR1/ERBB2/NF1/TP53); small HR-/HER2+ (n=70) and HR+/HER2+ (n=132) subgroups; 144 patients contribute >1 sample (partial non-independence); no treatment-response or survival data, so actionability is pathway-level inference, not demonstrated efficacy.

da-18-5.answer:
FINAL ANSWER (Task DA-18-5)

Cumulative frequency of MAPK pathway alterations in post-hormonal therapy HR+/HER2- tumors:

    116 / 705 = 16.5%  (95% CI 13.7%-19.2%)

Cohort definition
- Receptor subtype from the sequenced sample: HR_STATUS = Positive AND OVERALL_HER2_STATUS = Negative -> 1,362 of 1,918 samples.
- Therapy exposure: any sample that is NOT a "Treatment Naive Primary" (i.e., all metastases plus "Post-Treatment Primary" and "Post-Neo Primary" biopsies), because no explicit endocrine-therapy column exists in the clinical file. Index group n = 705 (629 metastases, 40 post-treatment primaries, 36 post-neoadjuvant primaries); treatment-naive HR+/HER2- primary reference group n = 657.
- Positive control that this grouping captures endocrine exposure: ESR1 mutations 18.6% (131/705) in the post-therapy group vs 1.4% (9/657) in treatment-naive tumors.

Event definition
- MAPK pathway alteration = nonsynonymous SNV/indel (MAF) OR amplification (CNA = 2) OR deep deletion (CNA = -2) in a MAPK-pathway gene covered by the panel.
- Primary gene set (19 genes, canonical Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK cascade + direct regulators): KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, RAF1, ARAF, MAP2K1, MAP2K2, MAPK1, MAPK3, NF1, RIT1, SOS1, PTPN11, RASA1, SPRED1, SHOC2, RRAS, RRAS2.

Result and comparison (post-therapy HR+/HER2- vs treatment-naive HR+/HER2-)
- 116/705 = 16.5% vs 53/657 = 8.1%; OR = 2.24, Fisher exact p = 2.4e-06. The twofold enrichment supports MAPK pathway activation as an acquired/selected endocrine-resistance mechanism.
- Main contributing events in the post-therapy group: NF1 loss 6.0% (42 samples, mostly truncating), KRAS 1.7% (hotspot p.G12* plus amplification), RIT1 2.0% (mostly amplification), RASA1 1.4%, MAPK1 1.1%, RAF1 1.0%, SOS1 0.9%, BRAF 0.7%.

Sensitivity to gene-set breadth (same 705 samples)
- Canonical 10-gene RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cassette only: 47/705 = 6.7% (naive 5.0%, p = 0.21).
- Adding MAP3K1/MAP2K4: 203/705 = 28.8% (naive 23.0%, p = 0.016).
- Adding MAP3K13/14, DUSP4, ERRFI1, RPS6KA4 (25 genes): 215/705 = 30.5% (naive 24.5%, p = 0.015).
- Broadest MAPK + upstream RTK definition (45 genes, includes FGFR1 amplification at 17.6%): 415/705 = 58.9% (naive 42.0%, p = 5.8e-10) - upper bound only.
- Cohort-definition sensitivity: using primary-tumor receptor status (n = 762 post-therapy) gives 16.7% vs 8.0%; restricting to metastases only (n = 629) gives 16.4%. The ~16.5% estimate is robust.

Interpretation
Roughly one in six post-endocrine-therapy HR+/HER2- tumors (about 30% if the upstream MAP3K kinases MAP3K1/MAP2K4 are included) carries a genomic MAPK-pathway alteration, dominated by NF1 loss and RAS-pathway activating events; NF1-mutant tumors alone are the largest genomically defined, potentially MEK/ERK-inhibitor-targetable subgroup.

Key caveats
- Hormonal-therapy exposure is inferred from sampling context (no explicit therapy column), so some post-therapy tumors may have received chemotherapy only.
- Cross-sectional comparison of different patients, not paired serial biopsies: clonal selection vs de novo resistance cannot be distinguished.
- MAP3K1/MAP2K4 losses are frequent in both therapy groups and are biologically ambiguous as "activation" events.
- Targeted 474-gene panel; non-genomic MAPK activation (phospho-ERK) is not measured.

Files: analysis script mapk_analysis.py; per-gene table mapk_per_gene_posttherapy_HRposHER2neg.csv; full trace trace.md.
