da-4-1.answer:
NMF of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) composition in the GSE243013 NSCLC anti-PD1 single-cell atlas (1,254,749 cells; 243 patients; 51 annotated immune cell subtypes) identifies an OPTIMAL CLASSIFICATION AT k = 4 PROGRAMS.

METHOD (summary)
- Built a 243 x 51 patient x cell-type composition matrix (percentage of each patient's immune cells per subtype), variance-stabilized with the arcsine-square-root transform (Y = 100*arcsin(sqrt(p)); non-negative as required by NMF).
- NMF (scikit-learn, NNDSVDa init, Frobenius/coordinate-descent, max_iter 1000, tol 1e-5); rank scan k = 2..8 with 100 restarts per rank; consensus matrices scored by cophenetic correlation (Brunet 2004) and dispersion (Kim & Park 2007); rank additionally judged by reconstruction-error elbow, 10%-masked cross-validated held-out error, program sizes, and clinical association.

WHY k = 4
- Consensus stability is near-perfect for all k <= 7 (dispersion 1.000 for k = 2..6, 0.9995 at k = 7; first instability at k = 8 with dispersion 0.83), so stability alone cannot pick k.
- Reconstruction error falls monotonically; the last double-digit relative gain is 2->3 (-15.7%) and 3->4 (-11.3%), then ~7% per factor (elbow after k = 4).
- Cross-validated held-out error has its optimum at k = 3-4 (RMSE 5.70 at k = 3, 5.88 at k = 4 vs 6.47 at k = 2 and 6.85 at k = 7).
- k = 4 has no singleton programs (sizes 4/31/100/108) and gives by far the strongest association with pathological response of any rank tested (chi-square p = 1.6e-08 vs p = 0.17 at k = 3 and p = 4.0e-03 at k = 5).

THE FOUR PATIENT CLASSES (n = 243)
- C1 Myeloid-rich (n = 4): MARCO+/VCAN+/FOLR2+ macrophages and cDC2 dominate; T/NK compartment compressed.
- C2 B-cell-rich (n = 31): naive/memory B (Bm_PDE4D, Bm_TNFSF9, Bm_CD74), plasma cells, germinal-center B (GCB_RGS13) - a B/TLS-like infiltrate.
- C3 Treg/exhausted-T (n = 100): expanded FOXP3+ Tregs (7.0% of all cells) and CCR8+ Tregs (3.8%), CXCL13+ and LAYN+ exhausted CD8 T cells.
- C4 NK/cytotoxic (n = 108): CD16hi FGFBP2+ NK cells (5.4%), CD8+ NK-like cells (4.0%), GZMK+ effector-memory and IL7R+ memory CD8 T cells, few Tregs (2.9%).

CLINICAL VALIDATION (pathological response, n = 242; 1 unlabeled patient excluded)
- 3-level response (non-MPR/MPR/pCR) x class: chi-square = 47.35, dof = 6, p = 1.6e-08.
- Responder rates (MPR + pCR vs non-MPR): C1 0/4 (0%); C2 22/31 (71.0%, OR 2.33, 95% CI 1.03-5.30); C3 30/99 (30.3%, OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.54, Fisher p = 1.1e-09); C4 78/108 (72.2%, OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.38-7.08, Fisher p = 2.0e-07). Overall responder rate 130/242 (53.7%).
- Continuous loadings show the same dose-response: P3 loading vs responder Spearman rho = -0.37 (p = 2.2e-09); P4 rho = +0.41 (p = 4.1e-11); Mann-Whitney p = 1e-33 to 1e-36.
- Robust to histology: effect holds separately in LUAD (C3 7% vs C4 57% responders, p = 1.5e-04) and LUSC (C3 39% vs C4 76%, p = 1.4e-05), and in regression adjusted for histology (P3 beta = -0.54, p = 1e-04; P4 beta = +0.34, p = 7e-04; LUSC beta = -0.23, p = 6e-04).
- No confounding by cells sampled per patient (rho = -0.07, p = 0.26), age, gender, smoking history, stage, treatment cycles, or radiological response (all p > 0.2).
- Replicated on raw percentages without the transform (p = 1.7e-05 at k = 4); the P3/P4 axis is recovered within responders only (k = 2 NMF inside the 142 MPR/pCR patients correlates r = 0.795 with P4), ruling out a response/cell-count artifact.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
The optimal NMF classification is a parts-based, lineage-archetype partition of the TIME along two axes: an immune-cold myeloid-suppressive pole (C1, MARCO+ macrophage-dominated) and, within lymphocyte-rich tumors, a T-cell-state pole separating Treg-enriched, terminally exhausted (CXCL13+/LAYN+) infiltrates (C3) from NK/cytotoxic effector-rich infiltrates (C4), with a B-cell/TLS-like class (C2) in between. The 2.4-fold responder-rate gap between C4 (72%) and C3 (30%) is consistent with Treg-mediated suppression and T-cell dysfunction opposing the NK/cytotoxic effector program that anti-PD1 therapy acts on, and the B-rich class aligns with tertiary-lymphoid-structure/B-cell predictors of checkpoint response.

ANSWER IN ONE LINE
The optimal NMF-based patient classification of this NSCLC anti-PD1 cohort uses k = 4 tumor immune microenvironment programs - myeloid-rich (n = 4), B-cell-rich (n = 31), Treg/exhausted-CD8-rich (n = 100), and NK/cytotoxic-effector-rich (n = 108) - and the resulting classes predict pathological response (chi-square p = 1.6e-08): NK/cytotoxic-rich patients respond at 72% while Treg/exhausted-rich patients respond at 30% (OR 4.1 vs 0.32), an effect that persists within LUAD and LUSC and after adjustment for histology.

MAIN LIMITATIONS
Analysis uses provided cell-level annotations (composition-level, no expression re-analysis); stability diagnostics saturate so k = 4 rests on elbow + cross-validation + interpretability + external association rather than a stability optimum (cross-validated minimum is technically k = 3); C1 is small (n = 4); histology, regimen composition, and other residual confounders are reduced but not eliminated; the design is observational and pre-treatment, so the class-response link is predictive, not causal.
da-4-1.notes: The analysis is strong overall, with a principled NMF workflow, robust stability assessment, dual justification for k=4, and thorough clinical interpretation; the main deductions are lack of cell-count filter and a single-initialisation final model.

da-4-6.answer:
Approximately 50% of non-MPR patients have high Texp cell levels that predict favorable recurrence-free survival despite lack of pathological response.

Definition: high Texp = Texp.in.Tex.relevant >= 8.05 (the median of the non-MPR stratum; column Texp.in.Tex.relevant*10 in mmc5.csv). Among the 70 non-MPR patients, 64 have a measurable Texp score, and 32/64 (50.0%; Wilson 95% CI 38.1-61.9%) are Texp-high (32/70 = 45.7% of all non-MPR patients).

Evidence that these high-Texp non-MPR patients have favorable RFS: 18-month RFS 86% (4/32 recurrences) vs 46% (17/32) in Texp-low non-MPR patients; median RFS not reached vs 15.8 months; log-rank p = 3.9e-4; Cox HR = 0.17 (95% CI 0.06-0.52), p = 0.0017; continuous model HR = 0.42 per +1 unit (p = 2.3e-5). The effect is robust across alternative thresholds (fixed 8.0: HR 0.16; Youden 7.36: HR 0.22; maximum log-rank 6.76: HR 0.14; all log-rank p < 3e-4) and persists after adjustment for stage, histology, residual disease (PRR_group) and adjuvant immunotherapy (adjusted HR 0.19, p = 0.0039). The prognostic signal is specific to the Texp state score (correlate of the CXCL13+ exhausted-CD8/module3 tumor microenvironment), not to TCR clonal burden (numberTexClone, top-3 clone sizes) or bulk Tex-subset fractions, which are null (p >= 0.16).

Range across definitions: 50% (median cut) to 81% (maximum-log-rank cut 6.76); 60% when restricted to patients with >= 12 months follow-up. Roughly half to two-thirds of non-MPR patients therefore carry a pre-treatment exhausted-T-cell state that marks durable recurrence-free survival despite residual disease, while the Texp-low half accounts for 81% (17/21) of non-MPR recurrences.
da-4-6.notes: The agent performed a rigorous analysis of non-MPR Texp stratification but did not include the required MPR comparison group, so several survival and hazard-ratio criteria are only partially met.

da-4-7.answer:
Answer: Which expanded Tex-relevant TCR clonotypes are shared across multiple patients (public) and could serve as TCR-T candidates?

METHOD (from GSE243013_T_with_TCR_annotation.csv.gz, 434,458 T cells / 231 NSCLC patients, joined to mmc1.csv clinical data):
- Tex-relevant = clonotype has cells in CD8T_Tex_HAVCR2 (progenitor-exhausted) and/or CD8T_terminal_Tex_LAYN (terminally exhausted) compartments.
- Expanded = clonotype flagged "expanded" in the data (equivalent to >=3 cells; verified: min cells of expanded = 3, max of non-expanded = 2).
- Shared across patients: clonotype IDs are patient-private (0/255,451 IDs occur in >1 patient), so sharing was assessed on the receptor-defining amino-acid TRB CDR3 sequence; candidates with an identical TRB+TRA CDR3 pair across patients are flagged as the strongest evidence (fully public alpha-beta receptors).

FILTER FUNNEL: 434,458 cells -> 41,337 Tex cells (31,093 HAVCR2+ + 10,244 LAYN+) -> 5,581 expanded Tex-relevant clonotypes (5,298 unique TRB CDR3 sequences) -> 35 sequences shared by >=2 patients (39 patients total; 14 of them with co-shared TRB+TRA CDR3 pairs).

TOP-RANKED CANDIDATES:

Tier 1 - broadest sharing (>=3 patients):
1. CASSLGYEQYF (TRBJ2-7; TRBV11-2/TRBV19/TRBV27/TRBV28/TRBV5-4 by patient) - 5 patients (P268, P289, P453, P470, P471), 33 cells, 58% in Tex (15 CD8T_Tex_HAVCR2, 4 CD8T_terminal_Tex_LAYN), expanded in all 5 patients; patient responses: 2x pCR, 1x MPR.
2. CASSLTLNTEAFF (TRBJ1-1; TRBV11-3/TRBV27/TRBV28) - 3 patients (P103, P321, P528), 122 cells (largest multi-patient clone), 40% in Tex, 104 cells flagged CD8Texp; responses: pPR, pCR, nPR.

Tier 2 - fully public alpha-beta receptors (identical TRB CDR3 + TRA CDR3 in 2 patients; strongest TCR-T target evidence):
- CASSPGPGGTEAFF / CAMSDLGAGAGSYQLTF (TRBV5-5+TRBJ1-1) - 130 cells, 45% Tex (P199 MPR, P200 pCR)
- CASSVSGTGFLRQPQHF / CAAEMDSNYQLIW (TRBV6-2+TRBJ1-5) - 117 cells (P199, P200)
- CASSLAGGDEQYF / CAVKNTGGFKTIF (TRBV27+TRBJ2-7) - 339 cells, 73% Tex (P70 nPR, P71 pCR)
- CASSPTGTGLEGYTF / CALIIGFGNVLHC (TRBV4-3+TRBJ1-2) - 80% Tex, highest Tex purity (P70, P71)
- CASSMTSGPGETQYF / CAASDNWVSSTSYGKLTF (TRBV19+TRBJ2-5)
- CASSHPTDYNEQFF / CAAVGGTSYGKLTF (TRBV7-9+TRBJ2-1)
- CSAEPGSDTQYF / CAARNSNTGNQFYF (TRBV20-1+TRBJ2-3)
- CASSLGMANTEAFF / CALSVDNYGQNFVF (TRBV7-8+TRBJ1-1)
- CASSPGGGETQYF / CAASFNGDNNDMRF (TRBV18+TRBJ2-5)
- CASSLRSNEQFF / CVASGNTPLVF (TRBV7-9+TRBJ2-1)
- CASSLGQGEQPQHF / CAVQARGSGYALNF (TRBV27+TRBJ1-5)
- CASSLVSYEQYF / CALPTTGTASKLTF (TRBV5-6+TRBJ2-7)
- CATSRDAGTGDTDTQYF / CAVNPFSGGYNKLIF (TRBV15+TRBJ2-3)
- CSASVGSYEQYF / CVVNPNTDKLIF (TRBV20-1+TRBJ2-7)
(11 of these are shared between patients P199 and P200 - a large shared clonotype family.)

Tier 3 - large Tex-resident public clones (2 patients, TRA differs):
- CASSLGGNEQFF (TRBV28/TRBV7-9+TRBJ2-1) - 378 cells, 74% Tex (P404 pPR, P47 pCR)
- CASSLTSGSSYEQYF (143 cells), CASSPTGTGELFF (136 cells), CASSLGPYNEQFF (39 cells, 77% Tex), CASSPGGNTIYF (35 cells), CASSSGGYEQYF, CASSLSYEQYF, CASSLGGSYEQYF, and the remaining 2-patient sequences in public_expanded_Tex_TCR_candidates.csv.

KEY STATISTICS: Public sharing of expanded Tex clonotypes is rare - 35/5,298 (0.66%) vs 3.71% of non-expanded and 1.45% of expanded non-Tex sequences (Fisher exact: OR 0.172, p = 6.6e-46 vs non-expanded; OR 0.453, p = 4.6e-06 vs expanded non-Tex). All 35 sequences are expanded in every patient that carries them. Convergent recombination is evident (CASSLGYEQYF uses 5 different TRBV genes; 18/35 candidates use >1 TRBV, 17/35 have one consistent TRBV).

CAVEAT: No antigen/HLA/pMHC data are provided, so candidate specificity is inferred from clonal expansion + Tex localization, not proven; most candidates (33/35) appear in only 2 of 231 patients, and per-patient sequencing depth bounds the observable breadth. Antigen identification (e.g., pMHC multimer/yeast display) is the required next validation step before TCR-T development.

Full analysis trace: trace.md. Candidate table with all 35 sequences, V/J genes, per-patient cell counts, Tex-occupancy fractions, patient IDs and responses: public_expanded_Tex_TCR_candidates.csv.

da-5-1.answer:
Question: Which proteins are promising PDAC drug targets based on both significant tumor overexpression (vs normal, adj. p <= 0.01) and CRISPR-knockout dependency in matched cell lines (adj. p <= 0.01), considering druggability?

METHOD (from the provided CPTAC druggability tables):
Starting from 5,262 proteins in the integrated indicator matrix (Table S3A), I filtered:
  5,262 -> 1,431 proteins flagged PDAC=1 (significantly overexpressed in PDAC tumors vs normal AND significant CRISPR dependency in PDAC lineages)
       ->   222 that carry a druggability tier annotation (Tier1-Tier5)
       ->    49 at the highest tiers (Tier1/Tier2) that are NOT DepMap pan-essential genes (pan-essential knockouts are nonspecific fitness effects)
PDAC dual-positive proteins are significantly enriched for druggable targets (15.5% vs 8.4% elsewhere; Fisher exact OR=2.01, p=3.1e-13) and for Tier1 targets (OR=2.80, p=4.2e-05), and are enriched for non-essential genes (85.6% vs 68.8%; OR=2.79, p=5.1e-09). All 49 priority targets have at least one approved drug mapped to them (Table S2B); 21 of 49 have an approved drug with a cancer indication.

PROMISING PDAC TARGETS - TOP RANKED (Tier1/2, tumor-overexpressed + CRISPR-dependent, non-pan-essential):
Receptor kinases / signaling (approved drugs already exist):
  ERBB2 (HER2)   - trastuzumab, lapatinib, pertuzumab, T-DM1
  MET            - crizotinib, cabozantinib, capmatinib, tepotinib
  PDGFRB         - sorafenib, sunitinib, pazopanib
  MAP2K2 (MEK2)  - cobimetinib, trametinib, binimetinib
  CSF1R          - pexidartinib, sunitinib (PDAC-only in this dataset)
  DDR2           - regorafenib (PDAC-only)
  SRC, YES1      - dasatinib
  BTK            - ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib
  IKBKB (IKK-beta) - arsenic trioxide
Antibody-accessible surface / other Tier1 targets:
  NECTIN4        - enfortumab vedotin (ADC repositioning candidate)
  F3 (tissue factor) - tisotumab vedotin
  JUN (AP-1)     - arsenic trioxide
  MAP4           - paclitaxel/docetaxel binding
  TYMP, DPYD     - tipiracil; tegafur-uracil (fluoropyrimidine pharmacology, relevant to 5-FU-based FOLFIRINOX)
  ATIC, GART     - methotrexate, pemetrexed (antifolates; GART dependent in 8/8 cohorts)
  ALOX5, TXNRD1  - masoprocol; arsenic trioxide
Tier2 enzyme/surface targets:
  LDHA, SQLE, HSD11B1, PDXK, TPK1, RFK, COMT, VKORC1L1, F2, F11, PLG, ACE, GANAB,
  MMP7, ITGAV, ITGB1, ITGA4, COL1A1, ANO1, CACNA2D1, VDR, NFKB2, ACTN1, PLIN3,
  APOC3, C1S, PROCR, ATP2C1

SECONDARY WATCHLIST (Tier3-5 but strongly PDAC-selective or surface-druggable, dual-positive, non-essential):
  CLDN18 (Claudin-18.2)   - PDAC-only here; zolbetuximab is Phase III-positive in gastric cancer
  FAP (fibroblast activation protein) - PDAC-only here; stromal target of active clinical programs
  CA9 (carbonic anhydrase IX), SLC2A1/GLUT1 - hypoxia/metabolism surface targets
  PVR/CD155, CSPG4, SCARB1, CDH2, ADAM10 - surfaceome/immunomodulatory targets
  HSP90AA1 - HSP90 inhibitors
Genomic-driver support within PDAC: PDXK overexpression links to methylation (Spearman rho=-0.34, p=0.0012); ADAM9 and EPHB4 are druggable CNV-amplified, overexpressed PDAC drivers (FDR<0.006). KRAS itself passes both criteria (Tier1) but is DepMap pan-essential, so its dependency signal is nonspecific.

BOTTOM LINE: The strongest evidence-backed, druggable PDAC targets are ERBB2, MET, PDGFRB, MAP2K2, CSF1R, DDR2, SRC/YES1, BTK and IKBKB among kinases; NECTIN4 and F3 as antibody-drug-conjugate antigens; the metabolic enzymes TYMP/DPYD, ATIC/GART, LDHA, SQLE; and the PDAC-selective surface proteins CLDN18 and FAP as watchlist candidates. All were selected because they are both significantly overexpressed in PDAC tumors versus normal pancreas and required for PDAC-lineage cell-line fitness in CRISPR knockout screens, while having clear druggability annotations and, for the top group, approved drugs that could be repositioned.

CAVEATS: binary flags preclude recomputing effect sizes/p-values; CRISPR dependency reflects cell-line fitness, not guaranteed in-vivo efficacy (and FAP/COL1A1-type signals may be stromal); approved-drug mappings record approval for the target, not activity in PDAC; pan-essential genes (e.g. KRAS, TOP2A, RRM2) were deliberately deprioritized. Full analysis: trace.md; ranked table: results/ranked_t12_targets.csv.
da-5-1.notes: The agent performed a rigorous analysis with correct counts and many top candidates, but lost some points for not ranking by multi-cancer validation and for incomplete biological rationale and validation next steps.

da-6-2.answer:
Temporal dynamics of gene expression in rat vastus lateralis (SKM-VL) across 8 weeks of endurance training, and the sex-specific vs shared patterns (data: 766 training-regulated genes, MoTrPAC Nature 2024 supplementary table).

1) THE TIME COURSE IN EACH SEX
The number of genes with a significant expression change at each timepoint (timewise p < 0.05 vs sex-matched sedentary controls) grows with training duration in both sexes and is consistently larger in females:
- 1w: 145 genes (male) vs 220 (female), 33 shared
- 2w: 134 vs 329, 39 shared
- 4w: 176 vs 501, 107 shared
- 8w: 379 vs 532, 265 shared
Effect sizes are modest (median |log2FC| of significant genes 0.31-0.53) and up/down directions stay balanced (47-65% up) in both sexes. The male and female response profiles CONVERGE as training progresses: the correlation between male and female logFC vectors rises from r = 0.13 (1w) and 0.07 (2w) to r = 0.43 (4w) and 0.63 (8w), and among genes significant in both sexes the direction agreement rises from ~70% (1-2w) to ~99% (264/265 at 8w). Females mount a broader response at every timepoint (Fisher-combined p < 0.05 across the four timepoints: 614/766 females vs 379/766 males).

2) FIVE TEMPORAL ARCHETYPES (k-means on row-z-scored sex x timepoint logFC profiles; k=5; stable, mean ARI 0.997)
- C0 (n=153) - SHARED delayed-onset UP: flat at 1-2w, rises at 4-8w in both sexes. Overwhelmingly mitochondrial / oxidative phosphorylation genes (respiratory chain complex, aerobic respiration; g_SCS p < 1e-30). Examples: Ckmt2, Ckmt1, Atp6v1g2, Lgi3, Gpr88, Lamb3, mitochondrial Mt-co1/mt-Nd4l/Mt-atp8.
- C1 (n=203) - LATE REVERSAL UP / CONVERGENCE: males start negative (-0.28, -0.25 at 1-2w) and end strongly positive (+0.42 at 8w); females rise early and stay up. Enriched for angiogenesis and blood-vessel morphogenesis (p ~ 1e-6). Examples: Znf750, Hspb6, Apln (apelin), Fhl1, Ppm1e.
- C2 (n=104) - MALE-DOMINANT UP, females silent: male means +0.1 to +0.34 at all timepoints, female means slightly negative until 8w. Enriched for Z disc, myofibril, sarcomere. Examples: Ckmt1 (male +3.75 to +4.94, the strongest response in the dataset), sarcolipin Sln (male +2.44 at 8w vs female -1.54 at 2w), Iqgap2.
- C3 (n=79) - FEMALE-TRANSIENT UP / male down (most sex-divergent cluster, male-female profile correlation ~0.03): females spike at 1-2w (+0.40, +0.58) then return to baseline; males are negative throughout. Enriched for interstitial matrix, ECM structural constituent, fibrillar collagen. Examples: Tnmd (F +1.79 at 2w / M -2.46), Col11a1 (F +1.32 / M -2.00), Emilin3, plus proliferation markers Mki67, Prc1, Kif22, Iqgap3.
- C4 (n=227, largest) - SHARED PROGRESSIVE DOWN: both sexes drift to -0.23 to -0.26 by 8w. Enriched for endoplasmic/sarcoplasmic reticulum, carbohydrate catabolism, glycolytic process, muscle structure development. Examples: Bcat2, Prkag3 (AMPK gamma-3), Megf10, Adhfe1, Cpa1, Nmrk2, and Fos (AP-1 immediate-early, down in both sexes - resolution of the stress-response program).

3) SHARED VS SEX-SPECIFIC
The PREDOMINANT pattern is SHARED and biphasic: an early (1-2w) remodeling wave followed by a shared delayed build-up of oxidative-mitochondrial genes (C0) and shared progressive repression of ER/glycolytic/structural genes (C4); by 8w the sexes induce/repress largely the same genes (Jaccard 0.41, direction agreement 99%), differing mainly in breadth (532 vs 379 significant genes).
The genuinely SEX-SPECIFIC component is EARLY and TRANSIENT: direct male-vs-female contrast tests (Wald z on logFC differences, BH-corrected per timepoint) give 11 dimorphic genes at 1w and 47 at 2w, but ZERO at 4w and 8w. These early dimorphic genes are enriched for collagen/ECM terms (collagen trimer, collagen fibril assembly, p ~ 0.002-0.03) and are mostly stronger in FEMALES (Col11a1, Tnmd, Col8a2, Lox, Ltbp2, Meox1, Gdf11; a few male-higher: Tnfrsf12a, Slco4a1). A male-skewed myofibrillar program (C2) persists as a quantitative (not per-gene-significant) difference.
Corroborating non-transcript layers in SKM-VL: metabolomics mirrors the timeline (glutathione down ~-3.7 logFC at 8w in both sexes; acylcarnitines/lysophospholipids and 1-methylnicotinamide up), and immunoassay shows a female-skewed early VEGF/IL-6/MIP2/LIX response (VEGF up at all four female timepoints), consistent with the female early ECM/angiogenic archetype.

BOTTOM LINE: In SKM-VL, endurance training produces a small-magnitude (|log2FC| mostly < 0.5), bidirectional transcriptional remodeling that broadens steadily over 8 weeks. Females respond earlier and more broadly than males; the early female response is dominated by ECM/collagen, immune and angiogenic programs plus proliferation markers, while a male-biased myofibrillar/contractile program appears in parallel. From 4 weeks onward both sexes converge onto the same shared program - delayed induction of mitochondrial oxidative-phosphorylation genes and progressive repression of ER/glycolytic/structural genes - so by 8 weeks the response is predominantly SHARED in direction and identity, retaining only a quantitative female bias in the number of responsive genes. Formal statistical support for sex dimorphism (BH q < 0.05) is confined to the first two weeks.

da-6-5.answer:
Endurance training elicits a broad but non-uniform, coordinated molecular response across rat organs, organized into a few reproducible tissue axes.

EXTENT OF COORDINATION
- Of 279,002 sex x timepoint contrasts on 35,441 training-regulated features (all training FDR < 0.05), 100,775 (36.1%) are timewise significant (|z| >= 2); the result is threshold-insensitive (alternative definitions flag 35.2-36.9%, r >= 0.94 with the primary).
- Response breadth is highest in the contractile tissues: heart (46.0% of its contrasts timewise significant) and gastrocnemius (46.2%), vs colon 20.3% and spleen 25.5%. Effect magnitude shows the inverse pattern: BAT's significant contrasts are largest (median |log2FC| 0.99; mean 1.27), heart's smallest among major tissues (median 0.24).
- Coordination across molecular layers: RNA and protein effect sizes correlate strongly in glycolytic muscle (SKM-GN r = 0.81, n = 80 shared genes) and moderately in lung (r = 0.61), but weakly in heart (r = 0.13), WAT (r = 0.11) and liver (r = 0.29). Union across the 9 omic layers multiplies the detectable response 4-7x over proteome alone (e.g. LIVER 5,926 entities vs 1,039 proteome features); only ~50-100 genes per tissue are regulated at both RNA and protein level.
- Coordination across sexes is pathway-level, not feature-level: only 12.8% of features are timewise significant in both sexes at the same timepoint; overlap of significant sets is at or below chance in all 54 adequately powered tissue x assay cells (median 0.98x independence expectation; colon transcriptome Jaccard 0.20), yet oxidative-metabolism enrichments fire in both sexes.
- Oxidative-metabolism programs anchor the shared response: FAO genes enriched in BAT (OR = 17.6, q < 1e-4) and heart (OR = 11.0, q < 1e-4); OXPHOS/mito genes in BAT (OR = 11.5), skeletal muscle (SKM-VL OR = 12.6, SKM-GN OR = 6.1), colon (OR = 4.7) and kidney (OR = 3.5), all q <= 1e-3. The response keeps growing with training: feature counts peak at 8 weeks in 9 of 17 tissues (liver 4,434; adrenal 3,406; heart 2,397; BAT 2,394), while WAT, lung, small intestine and hippocampus peak at 1 week.

MOST SIMILAR TISSUES (Pearson r of mean log2FC over shared regulated entities, n >= 30 shared entities required; top pairs stable across timepoints and across significance-restricted vs unselected means, rank rho = 0.83)
1. KIDNEY - gastrocnemius (SKM-GN): r = +0.71, n = 188, 70% same direction - the top pair overall, present at every timepoint; both co-upregulate oxidative phosphorylation.
2. BLOOD - SPLEEN: r = +0.62, n = 325, 81% same direction - the immune axis; the two cluster alone at every wave except 4 weeks.
3. ADRENAL - subcutaneous WAT: r = +0.57, best-supported pair (n = 728); with LIVER and PLASMA they form an endocrine-adipose-hepatic cluster (hierarchical clustering, k = 8: {blood, spleen}, {adrenal, liver, plasma, WAT}, {cortex, heart}, {hippocampus, kidney, lung, gastrocnemius, VL muscle}, and singleton BAT, colon, hypothalamus).
4. CORTEX - HEART (+0.65) and HIPPOCAMPUS - SKM-GN (+0.64): brain and muscle share direction of response.
5. The two skeletal muscles are the most directionally concordant of all pairs (SKM-GN - SKM-VL, 93% same sign, r = +0.53); heart vs VL muscle is the most anti-correlated pair (r = -0.54) - cardiac and skeletal muscle adapt differently.

Globally 59% of scoreable tissue pairs are positive (median r = 0.27): coordination is real and pathway-anchored (oxidative metabolism, shared between kidney, muscle, BAT and heart; immune programs shared between blood and spleen; endocrine programs shared by adrenal, WAT, liver and plasma) but not uniform - BAT, colon and hypothalamus each respond idiosyncratically, and BAT inverts its FAO/energy-buffer signature between 1 week (+0.34 log2FC; phosphocreatine +3.28) and 8 weeks (-0.82; phosphocreatine +1.80).

Main caveats: the file is pre-filtered at FDR < 0.05 and assay coverage differs per tissue (liver 9 layers vs blood 1), so per-tissue response sizes are not comparable in absolute terms; pairwise correlations rest on shared-entity sets (median n = 83) and are mildly inflated by conditioning on significance (bounded by an unselected-mean replication); ovary, testes and vena cava lack timewise statistics and are excluded from time-resolved conclusions.

===================

Question: Which hypertension-associated metabolites show a statistically significant positive
correlation with systolic blood pressure within the 'Bread-spiker' group, after adjusting
for age and BMI?

Bread-spiker classification (per the task definition): 67 plain-Bread CGM meals (no
mitigator/preload) -> per-subject mean peak glucose rise (post-meal peak 0-170 min minus
mean pre-meal baseline -25..0 min, averaged across replicates) -> cohort median = 57.61
mg/dL -> 18 bread-spikers (XB16, XB19, XB20, XB21, XB33, XB42, XB48, XB59, XB62, XB68,

Testing: 65 hypertension-associated metabolites (curated from the study's own annotation:
renal/uremic solutes, NO/arginine-citrulline axis, kynurenine pathway, HPA/steroid and bile
acid axes, BCAA/aromatic amino acids, BP-linked lysophosphatidylcholines and PUFA,
methylxanthines) via OLS  log2(abundance) ~ Systolic bp + age + BMI  within the 14
bread-spikers. Criteria: p < 0.05 and beta_SBP > 0; ranked by p.

Only 4 metabolites pass the significance and direction criteria (there is no top-10 of
passing metabolites; the passing set is smaller than 10). Ranked list:

  1. Kynurenic acid  (tryptophan-kynurenine pathway)   beta = +0.0518 log2/mmHg, p = 0.0025, R2 = 0.68
  2. Threonine       (amino acid metabolism)           beta = +0.0159 log2/mmHg, p = 0.0080, R2 = 0.57
  3. Citrulline      (nitric oxide / urea cycle)       beta = +0.0094 log2/mmHg, p = 0.0212, R2 = 0.68
  4. Creatinine      (renal function marker)           beta = +0.0067 log2/mmHg, p = 0.0320, R2 = 0.57

If a top-10 ranked list of significant positive associations is required and the
hypertension-association restriction is relaxed to the full 702-metabolite scan, the
rank-5-to-10 positions would be filled by (all p < 0.05, beta > 0, age/BMI-adjusted):
Hydroxyhippurate(2) (p = 0.076) does NOT pass p < 0.05; the next full-scan positives are
Citrinin (p = 0.0012, annotated exogenous fungal toxin), Asp-Arg (p = 0.0020, dipeptide),
Pro-Phe (p = 0.0032, dipeptide), N-Acetylgalactosaminitol (p = 0.0032), Proline
(p = 0.0034/0.017), Medazepam (p = 0.0040, exogenous drug), Bis(p-nitrophenyl)phosphate
(p = 0.0077, exogenous), D-Malic acid (p = 0.0119), 3-Methyl-4-pentenoic acid (p = 0.0134),
cis-4-Hydroxyproline (p = 0.0137) - most of which are unannotated/exogenous library

Biological interpretation: in subjects with exaggerated bread-evoked glycemic excursions,
higher SBP is independently associated with higher circulating kynurenic acid (inflammatory
tryptophan-kynurenine flux, elevated KYNA reported in essential hypertension), citrulline
(NO-synthase substrate supply, positively associated with SBP in population cohorts), and

Caveats: n = 14; no metabolite survives Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction even within the

da-8-2.answer:
Interaction effect size between baseline insulin resistance status and the protein-vs-fiber preload contrast on rice peak glucose (mitigator challenge data, rice experiments):

PRIMARY ESTIMATE (subject-level, within-person):
- Interaction slope: +0.17 mg/dL peak glucose per SSPG unit (beta = +0.1697, 95% CI +0.031 to +0.308, p = 0.019, n = 19 subjects with SSPG).
- Standardized effect size: Pearson r = +0.53 (= standardized beta; bootstrap 95% CI +0.20 to +0.77; sign-flip permutation p = 0.006).

DERIVATION:
- For each of the 23 subjects who completed both rice pre-load arms, peak glucose = max CGM glucose (mg/dL) over 0-170 min, median-combined across replicates.
- delta_protein = Peak(Rice+Protein) - Peak(Rice) = -15.5 mg/dL (p = 0.005).
- delta_fiber   = Peak(Rice+Fiber) - Peak(Rice)   = -10.5 mg/dL (p = 0.089).
- Within-subject interaction contrast DID = delta_protein - delta_fiber, regressed on baseline SSPG (steady-state plasma glucose; higher = more insulin-resistant).

GROUP EFFECT SIZE (median SSPG split, 75 mg/L, of the 19 analytic subjects):
- Low-IR (n = 9):  DID = -18.35 mg/dL (protein pre-load blunts the rice peak ~18 mg/dL more than fiber).
- High-IR (n = 10): DID = +5.35 mg/dL (protein advantage abolished; fiber marginally lower peak).
- Difference = +23.7 mg/dL (95% CI +3.9 to +43.5, p = 0.022); Cohen's d = +1.16 (large).
- Using the cohort-wide SSPG median (107): difference = +21.5 mg/dL, p = 0.049, d = +1.01.

GROUP-LEVEL CONFIRMATION (linear mixed model, peak ~ arm x IR, random intercept per subject, all 31 SSPG-typed subjects, 132 replicate peaks):
- arm x IR interaction contrast [Protein:IR - Rice:IR] = +27.9 mg/dL (SE 10.9, z = 2.55, p = 0.011); +27.5 mg/dL (p = 0.010) restricted to the 23 dual-preload subjects.

SENSITIVITY:
- SSPG tertiles: mean DID -17.9 -> -8.1 -> +7.7 mg/dL (monotone with IR).
- Winsorizing peaks (5-95%): r = +0.537 (p = 0.018). Random-replicate peaks: r = +0.521.
- HOMA-IR instead of SSPG (n = 23): r = +0.16 (p = 0.46) - not significant.
- Incremental-AUC endpoint: r = +0.27 (p = 0.26) - same sign, not significant.
- Fat pre-load control (Rice+Fat vs Rice, same 19 subjects): r = +0.20 (p = 0.40) - the SSPG moderation is specific to the protein-vs-fiber contrast.

INTERPRETATION: Baseline insulin resistance moderates the mitigator effect - the peak-glucose reduction from a protein pre-load relative to a fiber pre-load shrinks by about 1.7 mg/dL for every +10 mg/L of SSPG (r = +0.53, d = 1.16 high- vs low-IR), crossing zero near SSPG ~ 140-150 mg/L. Protein pre-loading is the better mitigator only in insulin-sensitive individuals; in insulin-resistant individuals the two pre-loads are equivalent or fiber is modestly better.

CAVEATS: n = 19-31; SSPG missing for 4 of 23 dual-preload subjects; effect attenuates to non-significance under HOMA-IR or iAUC endpoints; dichotomization threshold changes the group difference (21.5-27.9 mg/dL range). Treat as hypothesis-generating.
da-8-2.notes: The agent's analysis diverges from the rubric's expected methodology in several key ways: it uses SSPG instead of DI as primary IR marker, computes peak glucose as absolute rather than baseline-subtracted, uses the wrong sign for the reduction, and employs mixed-model/continuous regression instead of a two-way ANOVA with interaction, yielding opposite significance conclusions.

The potato- vs grape-spiker contrast is dominated by gamma-glutamyl dipeptides and - most notably among lipids - the long-chain acylcarnitine C16:0 / L-palmitoylcarnitine (HMDB00222, KEGG C02990), which appears in the top 10 as three co-measured features (ranks 3, 6, 10; log2FC +0.21 to +0.24, raw p 0.051-0.076, strengthening to p=0.0017-0.0020 in the stringent potato-only vs grape-only arm) and is HIGHER in potato-spikers; the androgenic steroid sulfate 3beta,16alpha-dihydroxyandrostenone 3-sulfate (rank 9, log2FC +0.74, p=0.072) is also higher in potato-spikers.
